title: Fox assistant: read-only end-to-end user guide so Cáo answers every question about using vCraft (GH#227)
description:
## Problem
Asked "hướng dẫn cách sử dụng hệ thống" (how do I use the system), Cáo answers that it has no guide and tells the user to look for a "Hướng dẫn" or "Trợ giúp" section that does not exist. Its knowledge base (`docs/assistant-kb/`) only covers Bát Tràng, household registration, ordering, QR traceability and quotation, so it cannot explain the platform end to end (accounts, roles, every main flow, where each feature lives).

## Approach
- **Knowledge.** Add a complete read-only user guide to `docs/assistant-kb/` (vi + en), ingested by the existing worker (`apps/worker/src/assistant/reindex-cli.ts`, `processors/assistant/ingest.ts`) as `FAQ` sources:
  - overview and site map: every public page and its internal path (home, products, artisans/households, map, news, trace `/truy-xuat`, quote requests, account);
  - accounts: sign up, sign in, sessions, profile, privacy;
  - each role end to end: visitor/buyer (browse, search, quote request, bids, order, payment, delivery tracking), artisan/household (registration, studio, products, production log, media, bidding, order allocations), admin (moderation, audit log, dashboard, news, notifications);
  - state machines users see (quote request, bid, order statuses) and what each status means;
  - common problems and FAQs.
  Keep it in sync with the shipped features (SRS / ARCHITECTURE), and only link to real internal paths.
- **Routing.** Make sure `site_help` questions (classifier in `apps/api/src/modules/assistant/application/prompt.ts`, fast intents) retrieve these guides, including broad questions like "how do I use vCraft" and page-aware ones ("what can I do on this page", using `pagePath`).
- **Prompt.** Let Cáo give step-by-step, role-aware instructions with links, and stop inventing sections that do not exist. It stays strictly read-only: it explains how to do things, never does them, and never exposes private data.
- **Tests.** Retrieval/eval cases for a set of system questions (vi and en), and red-team tests still pass.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Cáo answers "how do I use the system" with a short end-to-end overview and links, instead of "I have no guide"
- [ ] Cáo answers step-by-step questions for each role and main flow (sign up, quote request, bidding, order, payment, delivery, traceability, household registration, studio, admin) with correct internal links
- [ ] No answer points to pages or sections that do not exist
- [ ] Stays read-only and keeps the guardrails (no actions, no private data); red-team tests pass
- [ ] Guides exist in vi and en and are re-indexed by the worker
- [ ] Typecheck, lint and tests pass; answers checked in a real browser
close_reason: Implementation committed, pushed and reviewed in PR #229; validation results and deployment limitations recorded in PR.

title: Auth: add a username at sign-up and sign in with username + password instead of email (GH#212)
description:
## Problem
Accounts are identified only by email:
- **Sign-up** (`apps/web/src/features/auth/register-form.tsx`) calls `supabase.auth.signUp` with email and password.
- **Sign-in** (`apps/web/src/features/auth/sign-in-form.tsx`, around line 79) calls `signInWithPassword` with email and password.
- **Validation** lives in `apps/web/src/features/auth/schemas.ts`.

The owner wants:
1. a **username** field on the sign-up form;
2. sign-in with **username + password** instead of email.

This also lets the demo admin sign in on production as `admin` (see the `DEMO_ADMIN_USERNAME` note below).

## Approach
- **Data model.** Add a unique, case-insensitive `username` column to `app_user`, with a MikroORM migration for both PostgreSQL and MySQL.
  - Rules: 3-30 characters, `a-z 0-9 . _ -`, stored lowercase.
  - Reserve words such as `admin`, `root` and `support` for seeded or system accounts only.
- **Sign-up.**
  - Add a username field with live availability feedback, validated in `schemas.ts` with vi and en messages.
  - Keep email: Supabase Auth still needs it for confirmation, password reset and Google sign-in.
  - Make sure the `app_user` row receives the username, either through `signUp` user metadata copied by the API on first login, or through an API endpoint.
- **Sign-in.**
  - The form asks for username and password.
  - Supabase only signs in by email or phone, so resolve username to email on the server: an API endpoint, for example `POST /api/v1/auth/resolve-login`, or a server action. Then call `signInWithPassword` with the resolved email.
  - The response must not reveal whether a username exists: same generic error, same timing, rate-limited, behind Turnstile as the forms are today.
  - Decide whether typing an email in the same field still works (recommended: accept either, so older accounts and support flows keep working).
- **Existing users and Google sign-in.**
  - Users without a username are asked to choose one after their next sign-in.
  - Backfill the seeded demo accounts: `admin`, `buyer`, `household`, `pending`.
- **Demo admin.**
  - The seed (`packages/database/src/seeders/demo/accounts.ts`) gives the admin account the username `admin`.
  - `scripts/demo-auth.mjs` keeps using `DEMO_ADMIN_PASSWORD`; `DEMO_ADMIN_USERNAME=admin` is documented in `.env.example` and `docs/demo/README.md`.
- **Admin MFA stays as it is** (`admin-mfa-gate.tsx`, the `aal2` check in the API auth guard).
- **Leave unchanged:** forgot password (still by email) and Google sign-in.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Sign-up requires a unique username with clear vi and en validation messages
- [ ] Sign-in works with username + password; wrong username and wrong password give the same generic error
- [ ] Username-to-email resolution is server-side, rate-limited, and does not leak whether an account exists
- [ ] Existing users without a username are asked to choose one; the demo accounts are backfilled (admin = `admin`)
- [ ] Migrations for PostgreSQL and MySQL; unit, integration and e2e tests updated; typecheck, lint and tests pass
- [ ] Verified in a real browser on production: register a new account, then sign in as `admin`
notes: 2026-11-07: production demo admin (demo.admin@example.com, id d3a10000-...0001) password reset to the DEMO_ADMIN_PASSWORD value in the local .env; DEMO_ADMIN_USERNAME=admin added to .env. Username login itself is not implemented yet: until this issue lands the admin signs in with the email. Admin MFA (TOTP) still applies.

title: Fox assistant widget in the bottom-right corner of public pages (GH#81)
description:
Mirror of GH#81.

`apps/web/src/features/assistant`: the floating Fox launcher and chat panel on every public page.

Requirements: FR-AST-01, 04, 05, 06, PLAN E15 (UX section)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Launcher bottom-right, safe-area aware, never covers CTAs or the map bottom sheet; hidden in Studio/Admin if it gets in the way; lazy-loaded outside the route JS budget
- [ ] Panel: 380 px popover on desktop, vaul bottom sheet on mobile sized by `visualViewport` so the keyboard never hides the input
- [ ] Visual feedback < 100 ms after sending: message appears, Fox switches to `thinking` with rotating fun facts (`assistant.thoughts.*`, ~30 vi/en lines ≤ 60 chars, no repeats per session); `talking` while streaming; `refuse` when blocked
- [ ] Tokens buffered and painted per `requestAnimationFrame`; citation cards with internal links; quick-question chips per page (home, catalog, map, QR landing, quotation); `pagePath` sent for context
- [ ] Copy, 👍/👎, retry on error, stop, new conversation; conversation kept in `sessionStorage`; rate-limited answers show a friendly countdown

title: Fox assistant API: streaming answers with guardrails and read-only tools (GH#80)
description:
Mirror of GH#80.

`POST /api/v1/assistant/messages` streams answers over SSE. Thin controller, logic in `AskAssistantService`. Principle: block real attacks, never block real users.

Requirements: FR-AST-02 … 05, FR-AST-07, BR-AST-01 … 04, PLAN E15 (intent routing and guardrail tables)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Intent routing: greeting/thanks/bye answered without the LLM (< 100 ms, accents, no accents, teencode, emoji); `datetime` via `get_current_datetime` (incl. lunar date); `weather` via `get_weather` (Open-Meteo, Bat Trang by default, VN-only geocoding, Redis cache 15 min, friendly fallback); site help/catalog/trace/village via RAG + `search_catalog`, `get_open_workshops` (Guest permissions); harmless chitchat answered briefly; expert out-of-scope politely declined
- [ ] `LlmClient` port with an OpenAI adapter (`OPENAI_CHAT_MODEL`), classification running in parallel with retrieval
- [ ] `GuardrailPipeline` (Chain of Responsibility): InputSanitizer → RateLimiter (Redis, per IP + session, e.g. 10/min, 60/day) → daily token BudgetGuard (circuit breaker ⇒ "the Fox is asleep") → InjectionClassifier (heuristics only add suspicion; the model decides) → OutputFilter (canary, PII mask, link allowlist, sanitized markdown, no external images, `max_tokens`)
- [ ] Retrieved documents and tool results wrapped as untrusted data; read-only tool allowlist with Zod-checked arguments and 3 s timeouts; no tool writes data
- [ ] Anonymous `AssistantMessageLog` (hashed IP, intent, blocked + reason, first-token latency, tokens, feedback), deleted after 30 days; feedback endpoint for 👍/👎
- [ ] Feature flag to turn the assistant off; unit tests for every guardrail layer and integration tests for the SSE endpoint with a mocked LLM
close_reason: All AC met: POST /assistant/messages streams SSE (text/event-stream), guardrails in application/guardrails.ts, read-only tools in application/tools.ts + catalog-tools.service.ts, OpenAI client in infrastructure/openai-llm-client.ts, unit tests alongside each.

title: vCraft first release build spec (GH#187)
description:
## Problem Statement

The vCraft team has completed eight decision tickets that resolve scope, domain model, approval/access rules, journals, quotation workflows, visual direction, technical architecture, and demo acceptance. The codebase has working prototypes and a monorepo with domain packages, contracts, API, frontend, and worker layers. The team now needs one unified implementation brief that names the entry seams for testing, establishes what each tier owns, and confirms the acceptance checks before build starts.

## Solution

Synthesize the eight resolved decisions into a single build spec that defines:
- One test seam per major workflow (guest QR-to-visit, buyer quotation, household publish, admin coordination)
- Module boundaries and owned responsibilities
- API contracts and state machines to keep or change
- Media and notification pipelines
- Demo acceptance matrix tied to grading criteria
- Deployment and fallback setup

The spec treats the domain rules, state machines, and tour sequences as verified from the prior decisions and focuses on implementation seams, concurrency invariants, and observable evidence.

## User Stories

1. As a QA engineer, I want to know the exact entry point for testing each guest/buyer/household/admin journey, so I can build repeatable e2e scenarios on the deployed URL.

2. As a backend engineer, I want to know which state machines stay unmodified and which need new transitions for decline-cascade, decline-cancels-order, and production cancellation, so I can update the domain layer without guessing.

3. As a frontend engineer, I want to know the polling intervals and what each TanStack Query refetch should trigger, so I can build the reactive UI without SSE.

4. As an infrastructure engineer, I want to know the demo database reset boundaries, Supabase connectivity fallbacks, and mail provider setup, so I can prepare the VPS and document the venue setup.

5. As the team lead, I want acceptance checks for Lighthouse, responsive, concurrency, database independence, and upload performance tied to frozen demo data, so I know exactly what to show in the defense and how long each check takes.

6. As a contract owner, I want to know which Zod schemas need to be added or changed for the narrowed quotation flow (no auto-allocation, manual division, whole-order cancellation), so I can sync frontend and backend on request/response shapes.

7. As a household representative in the UI, I want the publish-and-journal path to be testable from a phone in the e2e suite, so the demo script can show the complete household workflow.

8. As a media engineer, I want to know the exact worker job scope (image convert, QR render, outbox relay) and the MIME/size validation boundary, so I can scope the pipeline without overbuilding.

9. As a domain expert, I want the RFQ state machine transitions documented for the new rules (buyer cancellation before production, admin cancellation after production, decline cascade, no reassignment), so I can verify the machine against the resolved spec.

10. As an administrator in the demo, I want the coordination flow to show how to assemble a cooperative quotation from household contributions, confirm allocations, and mark receipt, so the script covers the admin journey end-to-end.

11. As a test architect, I want the seams between domain unit tests, API integration tests, and e2e scenarios defined, so I know where to put each check (unit: state machine races, integration: DB concurrency, e2e: UI flow).

12. As a developer, I want to know which ADR decisions are kept vs. narrowed (e.g., Redis/BullMQ narrowed to three jobs, SSE deferred, assistant removed), so I don't build features that are out of scope.

13. As a grading examiner, I want the acceptance matrix to show one row per journey step with what I see on screen and which role is acting, so I can follow the demo script and check off each requirement.

14. As a performance engineer, I want the demo pre-checks (Lighthouse 90+, zero full reloads, WCAG AA, 360–1440 responsive, 12 MB upload → 1.5 MB output) tied to frozen data and scripts, so I know what baseline to hit before exam day.

15. As a database engineer, I want the MySQL independence tests in CI and the compose mysql profile documented, so the team can verify portability without manual setup.

## Implementation Decisions

### Scope Summary (from vCRAFT-9hg.1, 9hg.7)

Release boundary: Live demo early January 2027, 3-person team, one VPS + Supabase free tier. Complete guest, buyer, household, and admin journeys with Bat Trang sample data. Deferred: full bilingual authoring, fox assistant, 3D/scroll story/advanced motion, MFA enforcement, CAPTCHA, multi-device sessions, price charts, outage banners, QR label PDFs, tour routing, ratings, reallocation. Retained: email verification, password recovery, role checks, artisan invite, lock, audit log, notifications, structured news, household map with text list, production journals with corrections, quotation requests, sealed offers, manual order split, progress tracking, concurrency safety.

### Domain Model (from vCRAFT-9hg.2)

Household: craft-producing unit under own public name. One designated representative account per household (may be artisan or administrator, not a maker by account action). Artisan: individual maker; named artisans need no account for credit. Product: identifies one object or one production batch, own journal and QR code. Workshop: physical location under household; map inclusion ≠ visitor permission. Production batch: objects of one design in one run, one product with shared journal and QR.

### Approval & Access (from vCRAFT-9hg.3)

Four separate claims: Household approval (gate to exhibition and quotation; does not mean sentences true or named artisans made objects). Certificate verification (admin reviewed one certificate; never appears unverified; not proof of genuineness). Journal integrity (published account not silently rewritten; events may not have happened as written). Physical authenticity (never claimed). Actors: guest (no account, public pages), buyer (registered, own quotations), household representative (one account for one household, not made maker), administrator (sample data, not household member). One role per account. Failure: rejection (nothing public), suspension (hides public profile/products/workshops, QR shows unavailable notice, private records stay visible), withdrawal (hides one product and journal), locking representative (freezes journals, published pages stay).

### Production Journals (from vCRAFT-9hg.4)

Entry: one stage, declared date, note, optional images. System records save time (ordering) and declared date (story). Fixed stages: clay, throw, dry, paint, glaze, fire, finish; may repeat or skip (skip requires reason). Corrections: append-only after publication; mistake fixed by new entry naming superseded entry; original and correction shown together. Hash chain: SHA-256 append-only kept. Detects change/deletion/reordering. Does not prove events happened or who made object. QR page states "Journal integrity" label only. Publication: appears only with published product, withdrawn with it. Unfinished may publish (labeled "in progress"). Invalid code, unpublished, withdrawn, or suspended household all return missing page.

### Quotation & Coordination Rules (from vCRAFT-9hg.5)

Quotation lifecycle: Buyer invites selected households, requests admin coordination, or both. Request requires design, positive quantity, unit, destination, required delivery, quotation deadline. Drafts editable; sent specs/dates fixed. Changes require cancellation and replacement. Deadline is any future time (no 24-hour minimum); required delivery follows. Acceptance checks version (refuses stale). Creates order awaiting allocation confirmations. Offers: one offer covers full quantity. Partial goes through cooperative assembled by assigned admin. Each invited household declares max quantity, unit price, promised date; no cross-request reservation. Admin composes within limits; cannot rewrite. Buyer sees households, shares, dates, one complete price. Internal prices private. Allocation and production: all confirm before production starts. Manual division table. Inadequate capacity prevents sending. One household starts direct; assigned admin starts cooperative. Representative reports completed quantity (zero to allocated), notes/photos. Allocation DONE requires full quantity. All DONE permits buyer or admin receipt. After production starts, only admin cancels unfulfillable order. Lateness keeps IN_PRODUCTION. Allocation decline cancels whole unstarted order. State machines: RFQ DRAFT→SENT→BIDDING→ACCEPTED→IN_PRODUCTION→DELIVERED|CANCELLED|EXPIRED. Quotation SUBMITTED→ACCEPTED|REJECTED|WITHDRAWN|LAPSED (with versions). Allocation PROPOSED→CONFIRMED|DECLINED→IN_PROGRESS→DONE|CANCELLED. Changes: rfq-state-machine add buyer cancellation before production, admin cancellation after start, decline-cascade. bid-state-machine retain revision/terminal, enforce via application. allocation-state-machine decline ends own AND triggers whole-order cancel.

### Exhibition Journey (from vCRAFT-9hg.6)

Variant A (market-wall base): continuous reading household → makers → object → journal → visiting → wholesale. Variant C (QR-first guest): seal/journal newest first, walk back to household and visiting with home link. Content order: household history, maker credit, object, evidence, visit, wholesale inquiry. Public news by household, not price grid. Maker credit: individual names; person posting is administration, not maker. Map: real map preferred; text list as accessible alternative. Motion: seal moment + short transitions, respects reduced-motion. 3D hero/scroll story out. Sample data labeled. Open fix: desktop/tablet spacing in A and C needs pass; vase-plate overlap must be verified gone.

### Technical Architecture (from vCRAFT-9hg.7)

ADRs 13-15 stand: Supabase Auth, Storage over S3, business Postgres, pgvector. Browser talks Supabase direct only for sign in/refresh/MFA. All business data through API. No Data API touches business tables. MySQL portability: dual-driver entities, CI tests on MySQL via Testcontainers, compose mysql profile. Postgres-only SQL in supabase migrations only. Contracts own boundary: Zod validates both sides, generates OpenAPI. Controllers thin. /api/v1, cursor pagination, RFC 9457, ETag on reads, version-checked writes, idempotency keys. Optimistic versioning: accept-bid and confirm-allocation in one transaction checking version; stale refused. Deployment: one VPS + Supabase. Caddy TLS and same-origin routing. VPS: web, api, worker, Redis. Supabase: Auth, Postgres, Storage. Local storage fallback. Package boundaries enforced: domain free of framework/ORM/workspace, web never imports database/api, UI no business logic. Media: worker (sharp) converts to AVIF/WebP, renders QR PDFs; API validates magic/size/MIME; stores per ADR-14. Notifications: in-app + email (SMTP). Mail is environment detail. Redis/BullMQ: three jobs (media, mail, outbox relay). Polling (TanStack Query). Reused: hash chain code, MapLibre, auth boundary. Removed: assistant module/Claude/Voyage at runtime (migrations stay), TipTap (plain text + sanitization), weather.

### Demo Setup (from vCRAFT-9hg.8)

Services: one VPS + Caddy + Supabase (Auth, Postgres, Storage). Cloudflare Tunnel backup. SMTP mail (no SDK). Sample: one buyer, one household rep, one admin, one pending. ~20 households, 200+ products (4–7 stages), 12 quotation requests across states, one split order across 4 households in production, 15+ news. One QR on real cup. Three pre-logged profiles: buyer, household (phone), admin. Demo sequence: QR scan → household approval/publish → workshop discovery → news → buyer quoting → admin coordination → allocation confirms → progress → receipt. Acceptance matrix: one row per step (step, what examiner sees, role). Checks (frozen data): Lighthouse 90+ on key pages, zero full reloads, WCAG AA, responsive 360–1440, keyboard-only QR path, 12 MB upload → 1.5 MB output, concurrency (two-tab race refused with error), database independence (CI Postgres+MySQL), backup/restore practiced. Safety: pnpm demo:reset refuses dev/prod, if external down show local + tunnel first.

## Testing Decisions

Unit tests (packages/domain/test): State machine transitions for new buyer cancellation before production, admin cancellation after start, decline-cascade (whole order). Allocation plan: no cross-request reservation, manual table exact coverage. Hash chain kept.

Integration tests (apps/api/test): Outbox concurrency expands to new events. Supabase guard verifies new actions. New test: two simultaneous accept-bid or confirm-allocation refused with STALE_VERSION. Database independence: CI matrix Postgres + MySQL (Testcontainers).

E2e tests (tests/e2e/specs): Guest (QR → trace → household → map+list → visit). Buyer (request → deadline → expiry → invite → bid → accept → confirm → progress → receipt). Household (login → publish → journal correction visible → approve). Admin (coordinate → assemble → manual table → confirm shares → start → progress → receipt). Seams: guest public page, buyer /buyers, household /studio (phone), admin /admin.

Pre-exam checks: Lighthouse 90+, responsive, keyboard, image upload compress, concurrency race, DB switch to MySQL, backup/restore practiced.

## Out of Scope

Social networks, real household pilot, retail/payments/shipping/invoicing/mobile apps, automatic allocation/Gantt/lateness/reassignment, 3D/scroll/assistant/bilingual, deliverable deployment/live identity/mid-release migrations.

## Further Notes

All eight decisions closed. Spec synthesizes into one build brief. Domain rules and journeys verified from prior decisions, not re-negotiated. Focus on entry seams, module ownership, concurrency, observable checks. Pre-exam checks on frozen demo data, not live guarantees. Demo script repeatable; external outage falls back to local build.

title: vCraft digital exhibition: product specification and technical direction
description:
## Destination

Agree a product specification and technical direction for the first usable vCraft release, a deployed INT3306 digital exhibition with representative sample data, working authentication, saved data, and complete journeys for the required roles. The map is finished when its decision tickets leave a clear implementation brief and no unresolved scope or architecture decisions.

## Notes

See existing map notes; unchanged by this session.

## Decisions so far

- Set the first-release scope and demonstration priorities /vCRAFT-9hg.1: Early Jan 2026 demo, 3 people, one VPS plus Supabase free tier. Complete guest, buyer, household, and admin journeys with Bat Trang sample data. Defer bilingual authoring, fox assistant, 3D/scroll story, and extra account/operations features.
- Define the household, maker, workshop, and product model /vCRAFT-9hg.2: Multiple makers and workshops per household, one representative account, and product identity per object or production batch with its own QR history.
- Define approval, publishing, and access rules /vCRAFT-9hg.3: One role per account; separate claims for approval, certificate verification, journal integrity, and no physical-authenticity claim; audience rules with an unavailable notice for old QR links.
- Define production journals and traceability guarantees /vCRAFT-9hg.4: Append-only after publication with visible correction entries, fixed seven-stage vocabulary with repeats and explained skips, declared date plus system time, the existing hash chain kept with a fixed one-sentence integrity limit, and the corrected failure table where locking freezes but does not hide.
- Define quotation and shared-order coordination rules /vCRAFT-9hg.5: One complete accepted offer, private household contributions, validated manual allocation, confirmations before production, quantity progress and explicit receipt; one strict deadline and whole-order cancellation instead of reassignment.
- Choose the exhibition journey, content, and visual direction /vCRAFT-9hg.6: A (market-wall reading) as base plus C (QR-first entry) for guests; confirmed content order; real map kept with text list as companion; closed-workshop card dropped; desktop and tablet spacing still need a pass before build.

• Choose the technical architecture and reuse boundaries /vCRAFT-9hg.7: ADRs 13-15 kept without reversal; narrowed worker, polling instead of SSE, MapLibre kept with heavy frontend dropped, hash chain and domain rules reused as is, optimistic versioning, in-app plus email notifications; assistant runtime, TipTap, and weather leave the release.
- [Define the deployed demo and release acceptance checks](vCRAFT-9hg.8): VPS plus Supabase demo with fixed accounts and Bat Trang sample data, one repeatable QR-to-delivery script, and pre-exam evidence for Lighthouse, responsive, upload, concurrency, independence, and recovery.

## Not yet specified

- Further decisions that retained optional features may introduce. First decide whether the features belong in the release before planning their details.
- Focused compatibility or service-limit investigations that may become necessary when the actual architecture alternatives are clear.
- Conflicts between the exhibition prototype, the final content set, and the intended demonstration experience that only become visible after those choices.

## Out of scope

- Social-network features such as follows, public comments, and a social feed. The agreed public experience is a digital exhibition; a later change in direction needs a new scoped effort.
- A pilot with real households and live wholesale orders. This release targets the course demonstration using representative sample data.
- Retail checkout, online payments, shipping integrations, electronic invoicing, and native mobile applications.
- Delivering the application, deploying services, collecting real identity documents, or executing database changes during this planning effort. Small local prototypes are allowed only to support a decision.
- Automatic allocation strategies, global capacity scheduling/reservations, Gantt charts, predicted lateness, and household reassignment are outside first-release coordination, as scoped in Define quotation and shared-order coordination rules /vCRAFT-9hg.5.
notes: Tracker operations, including the verified fallback for contributor routing, are documented in docs/agents/issue-tracker.md under Wayfinding operations. Shared vocabulary starts at root GLOSSARY.md. The user-approved charting scope is recorded by [Chart the vCraft product direction and first-release decision map](vCRAFT-clc).

title: Complete household request-info and applicant resubmission lifecycle
description:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

Source GH#249 s6-03. Audit reports REQUEST_INFO as a PENDING_REVIEW self-transition, no applicant resubmit action, stale statusReason and no queue signal. Keep state, applicant action, queue display and notification in one vertical slice. Estimate 4-6 hours after confirming whether a distinct state or explicit review marker preserves existing contracts.

## Steps to Reproduce

In local fixtures, request information for a pending household, edit the application as its representative, then inspect the admin queue before and after explicit resubmission. Compare badges, reason, review marker and notifications.

Out of scope: automatic approval, changing approved-household publication rules or public certificate verification. Original production claim not re-reproduced during import.
acceptance_criteria: Applicant sees requested information and can explicitly resubmit after edits. Admin distinguishes waiting-on-applicant from resubmitted applications and receives an actionable signal. Old reason is retained as history or cleared consistently rather than masquerading as an active request. Ownership, invalid transitions and repeated submission are tested.
notes:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

Static review: ProfileEditor is shown only to APPROVED households although updateProfile API permits PENDING_REVIEW and blocks REJECTED. REQUEST_INFO is a pending self-transition; statusReason persists. Need maintainer choice of explicit NEEDS_INFO/RESUBMIT states versus review timestamps/markers before unattended implementation. Ensure pending applicants can edit only their own application and resubmit with a clear queue signal.
Design choices are recorded on vCRAFT-8my and implementation is in progress. Deployed acceptance is tracked separately by vCRAFT-5nd; local checks do not establish production acceptance.
close_reason: Resolved under the user request. Pending applicants can edit profile/workshops, upload classified private evidence, and explicitly resubmit using the current version. Resubmit clears the active reason, preserves audit history, persists the review marker and notifies administrators with a review target. Typed evidence preserves private access/consent and deduplicated legacy UNKNOWN upgrades. Corrected lifecycle/media suites pass12tests on PostgreSQL and12onMySQL; main verified56targeted UI/auth tests and the full unit run passes18Turbo tasks including738webtests. title: Invalidate public household, product and trace views on suspension changes
description:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

Source GH#249 s6-07. Audit reports correct immediate API hiding but public pages remain stale for over 100 seconds, including stale warnings after reinstatement. Treat household/product/trace visibility as one consistency fix. Estimate 3-4 hours.

## Steps to Reproduce

In an authorized local/staging fixture, warm public household, product and trace pages as a guest. Suspend the household, compare API and web views immediately and after cache refresh, then reinstate and repeat. Include both locales and fresh/returning browsers.

Define the visibility consistency contract before changing cache behavior. Coordinate with GH#255 performance work so caching cannot restore suspended content.

Out of scope: changing suspension into account locking, deleting private records, allocation strategies GH#247 and blanket disabling unrelated caches. Production mutation not performed during triage.
acceptance_criteria: Public household/products hide promptly under the agreed consistency contract; trace shows the correct warning. Reinstatement removes stale warnings. Tests warm caches before each transition. Both locales agree with API authorization. Private household records remain accessible only to authorized actors; performance/cache effects are documented.
notes:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

Static review narrows the evidence: public household/product/trace routes are already force-dynamic, while exhibition fetch uses next.revalidate 30. No cross-deployment revalidate hook was found. Thirty seconds alone does not explain reported 100+ seconds. Inspect cache headers and deployment/version behavior and reproduce in controlled fixtures before selecting a remedy. Do not claim confirmed ISR root cause. Agree the immediate-visibility budget before final acceptance.
Design choices are recorded on vCRAFT-8my and implementation is in progress. Deployed acceptance is tracked separately by vCRAFT-5nd; local checks do not establish production acceptance.
close_reason: Resolved under the user request to finish 8my. Public moderation-sensitive detail/list/page/trace fetches use no-store on each server request, while redirects and village statistics retain their cache. Five targeted visibility/map tests pass, including warmed suspension/reinstatement cycles with both locale fixtures. The reported 100-second production mechanism remains unconfirmed; deployed acceptance is tracked by vCRAFT-5nd.

title: Diagnose API read and search-suggestion latency with comparable measurements
description:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

Merged sources GH#255 s8-08 and GH#254 s1-07. One owner must distinguish server, database, proxy, TLS and debounce costs. Link the GH#254 epic to this result. Suggestion target is <=300ms after the final keystroke with 150ms debounce; read target is p95 <=200ms at specified load. Original 10-client audit observed Cloudflare challenges, so it does not verify 100-user capacity or server processing latency. Estimate 3-4 hours for diagnosis and bounded remedies.

Use controlled local/staging timings, query analysis and comparable end-to-end measurements. Do not run production bursts. Preserve suspension visibility and ADR-0020 pagination when considering caches.

Out of scope: new search UI, unbounded infrastructure rewrite, production load tests and paid upgrades. No independent timing reproduction during import.
acceptance_criteria: Record p50/p95, sample count, concurrency, warm/cold state, location and server/database times for audited reads plus suggestions. Measure keystroke-to-visible-result separately. Distinguish transport/processing. Proposed caches cannot leak private or suspended content. Record bounded code fixes, infrastructure decisions and target compliance honestly.

title: Apply hosted Auth CAPTCHA, password, SMTP and token settings
description:

Source GH#238 s0-01, hosted s3-03, SMTP s3-04 and s3-10. useCaptcha already passes captchaToken; an empty public key disables it. Local config has jwt_expiry 900 but 8-character letters_digits policy and local CAPTCHA disabled. Reuse existing CAPTCHA. Production needs matching CAPTCHA keys and server enforcement, application-aligned password rules, leaked-password protection if available, 900-second access JWTs and functioning custom SMTP. Record provider limitations for maintainer resolution. Compare settings first. Never put secrets in tickets.

Out of scope: wholesale config push or enforcing CAPTCHA locally. Production changes require authorization in the implementation session. No hosted settings verified during triage.
acceptance_criteria: Record sanitized before/after settings. Reject missing/invalid CAPTCHA server-side and verify valid flows. Verify exp minus iat equals 900 without storing tokens. Check session refresh and mail delivery. Verify provider password rules and leaked-password availability. Browser checks at 360px and 1440px.
notes:
Hosted configuration is blocked on owner access to Cloudflare, Vercel, Supabase management settings and SMTP. No management tokens or Turnstile keys are available in this session. title: Web and API performance budget audit follow-up (GH#255)
description:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

Source: https://github.com/DienHung05/vCRAFT/issues/255

Imported for mad-uet. Source tracking epic; implement bounded children. Audit evidence is from 2026-11-07 and was not re-reproduced during import. No source comments. Close after all findings and deployed acceptance are resolved. Performance work must preserve suspension visibility and ADR-0020 pagination.

## Problem

NFR-PERF-01/02/03/05 fail on production (Lighthouse mobile, median of 3 runs; light API sample with 10 concurrent clients). The home page scores 99/100/100/100.

Found by the end-to-end system test of production (https://vcraft-vn.vercel.app, branch `main`, 2026-11-07) against `docs/SRS.md` and `docs/requirements/vCraft.pdf`. Each item was reproduced at least twice unless noted.

Requirements: `NFR-PERF-01`, `NFR-PERF-02`, `NFR-PERF-03`, `NFR-PERF-05`, `NFR-PERF-06`

## Findings

### Products list: Lighthouse mobile Performance 75 (LCP 8.0 s) because the above-the-fold product images are loading=lazy with no priority
`s8-03` · P2 · NFR-PERF-01, NFR-PERF-02, NFR-PERF-06 · reproduced 2x

- **Where:** /vi/san-pham
- **Expected:** Performance >= 90, LCP <= 2.5 s (NFR-PERF-01/02).
- **Actual:** Performance 75/76/75 (median 75), LCP 8.1/7.9/8.2 s, FCP 1.2 s, TBT < 20 ms, CLS 0.001. The LCP element is a product-card image in the first viewport (img loading=lazy, no fetchpriority, LCP discovery audit 0, resource load delay 0.7-0.9 s). Home (99) and trace (100) pass.
- **Suspected cause:** Card images on the catalog grid are all lazy; the first row(s) should be eager (loading=eager + fetchpriority=high on the first card images). Images are served from supabase.co (cross-origin) while the trace/home heroes use /media-cache.

<details><summary>Steps to reproduce</summary>

1. Run Lighthouse mobile 3 times on https://vcraft-vn.vercel.app/vi/san-pham (cold and warm)

</details>

### Initial JavaScript per route is 290-810 KB (brotli) on every page, far above the 180 KB gzip budget
`s8-04` · P2 · NFR-PERF-05 · reproduced 2x

- **Where:** all routes
- **Expected:** <= 180 KB gzip initial JS per route; 3D scene, map and editor lazy-loaded (NFR-PERF-05).
- **Actual:** Brotli transfer for scripts: sign-in/forgot/privacy ~475 KB, home 514 KB (mobile) / 785 KB (desktop, three.js chunk 245 KB), products 507 KB, product 475 KB, news 612 KB, map 809 KB (maplibre 296 KB), trace 289 KB (lowest). Before the window load event: login 409 KB, products 336 KB, trace 267 KB. Heavy shared chunks (gzip): react-dom 72 KB, @supabase client 61 KB (also on guest pages), zod 40 KB, assistant drawer (radix+vaul) 29 KB.
- **Suspected cause:** Supabase client and zod are bundled into the shared client chunk used by every route; the heavy libraries are lazy but still fetched right after hydration.

<details><summary>Steps to reproduce</summary>

1. Load each page with cache disabled on a mobile viewport and sum the encoded size of all script responses (CDP Network.loadingFinished)

</details>

### API read latency far above NFR-PERF-03: p50 0.7-2.5 s and p95 1.1-3.2 s with 10 concurrent clients; one 502 observed
`s8-08` · P2 · NFR-PERF-03 · reproduced 1x

- **Where:** GET /api/v1/products, /products/:slug, /households, /households/:slug, /map/workshops, /trace/:code
- **Expected:** Read p95 <= 200 ms (at 100 concurrent users).
- **Actual:** Single warm requests ~0.4-0.5 s from this network (curl, new TLS connection each). With 10 concurrent: products list p50 1.1 s / p95 3.2 s; product detail 0.9/2.3 s (one 502); households 2.5/3.2 s; household detail 1.0/2.1 s; map workshops 0.7/1.8 s; trace 0.9/1.2 s. Cloudflare returned a 429 managed challenge (cf-mitigated: challenge) to this IP for a few minutes after the burst.
- **Suspected cause:** Render free instance (single small CPU); responses are not cacheable (cf-cache-status DYNAMIC).

<details><summary>Steps to reproduce</summary>

1. 35 requests per endpoint (5 sequential then 10 workers x 3), 216 total, concurrency 10
2. See (local evidence)

</details>

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Fixed: Products list: Lighthouse mobile Performance 75 (LCP 8.0 s) because the above-the-fold product images are loading=lazy with no priority (`s8-03`)
- [ ] Fixed: Initial JavaScript per route is 290-810 KB (brotli) on every page, far above the 180 KB gzip budget (`s8-04`)
- [ ] Fixed: API read latency far above NFR-PERF-03: p50 0.7-2.5 s and p95 1.1-3.2 s with 10 concurrent clients; one 502 observed (`s8-08`)
- [ ] Verified on production in a real browser at 360 px and 1440 px; typecheck, lint and tests pass
design: Keep image LCP, shared initial JavaScript and API latency separate so changes have attributable measurements. GH#254 s1-07 is owned by vCRAFT-va0.3, not a duplicate search-performance ticket. Public caching must preserve suspension behavior from GH#249 and ADR-0020 page/cursor semantics. Coordinate shared component edits serially when implementation sessions overlap.

title: Public catalog and search audit follow-up (GH#254)
description:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

Source: https://github.com/DienHung05/vCRAFT/issues/254

Imported for mad-uet. Source tracking epic; implement bounded children. Audit evidence is from 2026-11-07 and was not re-reproduced during import. No source comments. Close after all findings and deployed acceptance are resolved. Search latency overlaps GH#255 and must have one performance owner.

## Problem

FR-CAT-02/04/05/07/08 gaps on production. Filtering, sorting, paging and diacritic-insensitive search otherwise pass.

Found by the end-to-end system test of production (https://vcraft-vn.vercel.app, branch `main`, 2026-11-07) against `docs/SRS.md` and `docs/requirements/vCraft.pdf`. Each item was reproduced at least twice unless noted.

Requirements: `DR-03`, `FR-CAT-02`, `FR-CAT-04`, `FR-CAT-05`, `FR-CAT-07`, `FR-CAT-08`, `NFR-PERF-03`

## Findings

### Catalog filter 'has open workshop' and sort 'popular' do not exist (UI and API)
`s1-05` · P2 · FR-CAT-02 · reproduced 2x

- **Where:** https://vcraft-vn.vercel.app/vi/san-pham
- **Expected:** FR-CAT-02: filters category, household, price range, one-of-a-kind, in stock, has open workshop; sorts newest, price, popular.
- **Actual:** Two of the required options are absent. All other filters and sorts are correct against API data (see matrix), sync to the URL, give identical results in a fresh context and load by fetch without reload.
- **Suspected cause:** packages/contracts/src/catalog/index.ts:12 PRODUCT_SORTS has no 'popular'; ListProductsQuerySchema (line 19-30) has no open-workshop flag.

<details><summary>Steps to reproduce</summary>

1. Open the filter bar: category, household, price from/to, sort (Moi nhat / Gia tang dan / Gia giam dan), Doc ban, Con hang
2. GET /api/v1/products?sort=popular -> 422
3. GET /api/v1/products?openNow=true -> parameter silently ignored (returns the full list)

</details>

### Ctrl K / Cmd K only focuses the header search box: no command palette, no category suggestions, news suggestions link to the list
`s1-06` · P2 · FR-CAT-04 · reproduced 2x

- **Where:** https://vcraft-vn.vercel.app/vi
- **Expected:** FR-CAT-04: instant suggestions across products, households, categories and news in a command palette (Cmd K / Ctrl K).
- **Actual:** Header-box dropdown instead of a palette; categories are missing (searching 'Do tho' returns no category entry, and product search by category name returns 0); news suggestion links ignore the slug. Mobile has no Ctrl K (search lives in the Menu panel). Diacritic-insensitive matching works ('bat trang' = 'Bat Trang' = 'BAT TRANG', 'binh hut loc' finds 'Binh hut loc').
- **Suspected cause:** apps/web/src/features/catalog/search-box.tsx:62-70 (focus only), :172 (href="/tin-tuc"); catalog.service.ts suggest() has no category source.

<details><summary>Steps to reproduce</summary>

1. Press Ctrl+K on any desktop page: the header input gets focus, no dialog opens
2. Type 'do tho' or 'binh': dropdown groups are Products, Households, News only
3. Click a News suggestion: it goes to /vi/tin-tuc (list), not to the article

</details>

### Search suggestions appear about 450 ms after the last keystroke, above the 300 ms target
`s1-07` · P3 · FR-CAT-04, NFR-PERF-03 · reproduced 5x

- **Where:** https://vcraft-vn.vercel.app/vi
- **Expected:** FR-CAT-04: suggestions visible after <= 300 ms (debounce 150 ms).
- **Actual:** 430-471 ms in all 5 runs (about 150 ms debounce + 280-320 ms of network through the Vercel rewrite to Render; API alone 380-560 ms from curl, 1.29 s once for 'tra'). Warm API.
- **Suspected cause:** Network latency of the web -> Render hop; no caching on /search/suggest.

<details><summary>Steps to reproduce</summary>

1. Desktop, header search, type 'bat trang', 'binh hut', 'am chen', 'gom minh hai' (5 runs)
2. Measure from the last keystroke to the panel content

</details>

### Product detail has no gallery zoom and no QR code
`s1-08` · P2 · FR-CAT-05 · reproduced 2x

- **Where:** https://vcraft-vn.vercel.app/vi/san-pham/binh-hut-loc-men-lam-bt7k2qxm
- **Expected:** FR-CAT-05: gallery with zoom, info, production log summary, QR, more from the same household.
- **Actual:** One static cover image (every sampled product has images: [] so only the cover exists; extra thumbnails only appear for journal-entry photos, none seeded). Click does nothing (no dialog, cursor auto). No QR on the page, only the trace code text and a 'Xem hanh trinh' link. Info, log summary (7 entries, dated) and 'Cung ho nay lam' are present. Price format 4.800.000 d correct.
- **Suspected cause:** apps/web/src/app/[locale]/(discover)/san-pham/[slug]/page.tsx:97-137 renders one ImageSlot, no zoom/lightbox/QR component.

<details><summary>Steps to reproduce</summary>

1. Open the product page, click the photo
2. Look for a QR block

</details>

### English pages show Vietnamese material, dimensions and description for products, and demo data seed has only 42 distinct product names for 218 products
`s1-14` · P3 · FR-CAT-08, DR-03 · reproduced 2x

- **Where:** https://vcraft-vn.vercel.app/en/products/binh-hut-loc-men-lam-bt7k2qxm
- **Expected:** FR-CAT-08 vi/en site; credible catalog.
- **Actual:** Material 'Dat set trang Truc Thon...', dimensions 'Cao 32 cm...', description and name stay Vietnamese in /en. USD reference price present and correct (4.8M VND = US$187 at 25,630). Catalog: each of 42 names repeats about 6 times across households with unrelated prices (same name 300,000 d and 4,800,000 d), so a search for 'binh hut loc' returns 11 identical titles.

<details><summary>Steps to reproduce</summary>

1. Open the English product page
2. Count distinct names in /api/v1/products

</details>

### Favourites list (FR-CAT-07) is not implemented
`s1-13` · P3 · FR-CAT-07 · reproduced 2x

- **Where:** https://vcraft-vn.vercel.app/vi/san-pham
- **Expected:** FR-CAT-07 (Could): favourites stored locally for guests, synced after sign-in.
- **Actual:** No UI, no API.

<details><summary>Steps to reproduce</summary>

1. Look for a heart/save control on product cards and detail pages; grep of apps/web, apps/api and contracts finds no favourites code

</details>

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Fixed: Catalog filter 'has open workshop' and sort 'popular' do not exist (UI and API) (`s1-05`)
- [ ] Fixed: Ctrl K / Cmd K only focuses the header search box: no command palette, no category suggestions, news suggestions link to the list (`s1-06`)
- [ ] Fixed: Search suggestions appear about 450 ms after the last keystroke, above the 300 ms target (`s1-07`)
- [ ] Fixed: Product detail has no gallery zoom and no QR code (`s1-08`)
- [ ] Fixed: English pages show Vietnamese material, dimensions and description for products, and demo data seed has only 42 distinct product names for 218 products (`s1-14`)
- [ ] Fixed: Favourites list (FR-CAT-07) is not implemented (`s1-13`)
- [ ] Verified on production in a real browser at 360 px and 1440 px; typecheck, lint and tests pass
design: Scope mapping: s1-05 workshop filter=.3 and popular=.4; s1-06 suggestion contract/news links=.1 and palette=.2; s1-07 has one owner vCRAFT-va0.3 under GH#255; s1-08 QR+zoom merged=.5; s1-14 English model=.6, UI=.7, seed quality=.8; s1-13 guest favourites=.9 and sync=.10. QR and zoom share one detail-page test pass and remain <=6h. Keep independent catalog filter/ranking decisions separate. Preserve ADR-0020 totals and existing trace identity. English and favourites require complete model/UI dependencies before parent closure.

title: Household moderation and admin audit follow-up (GH#249)
description:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

Source: https://github.com/DienHung05/vCRAFT/issues/249

Imported for mad-uet. Source tracking epic; implement bounded children. Audit evidence is from 2026-11-07 and was not re-reproduced during import. No source comments. Close after all findings and deployed acceptance are resolved.

## Problem

FR-ADM-02..06 gaps found while approving, rejecting and suspending test households on production.

Found by the end-to-end system test of production (https://vcraft-vn.vercel.app, branch `main`, 2026-11-07) against `docs/SRS.md` and `docs/requirements/vCraft.pdf`. Each item was reproduced at least twice unless noted.

Requirements: `FR-ADM-02`, `FR-ADM-03`, `FR-ADM-04`, `FR-ADM-05`, `FR-ADM-06`

## Findings

### Suspended household stays publicly visible on household/product/trace pages for 100+ seconds (stale page cache)
`s6-07` · P2 · FR-ADM-04 · reproduced 3x

- **Where:** /vi/nghe-nhan/{slug}, /vi/san-pham/{slug}, /vi/truy-xuat/{code}
- **Expected:** FR-ADM-04: the household's products disappear from the catalog and the QR trace page shows the warning right after the suspension.
- **Actual:** In two 110 s polling runs the household page, product page and trace page kept rendering the pre-suspension content (HTTP 200, title with the household/product name, 'Ban vua quet an cua ...') although the API returned 404 the whole time. Once (Playwright, authenticated) the trace page showed the warning correctly but the household page still showed the full profile, and after reinstating the trace page still showed the suspension warning. The catalog API itself is correct (product list hides the product at once).
- **Suspected cause:** apps/web/src/features/catalog/exhibition-api.ts:34 (fetch next.revalidate 30) combined with full-route/ISR caching of the public pages; not confirmed

<details><summary>Steps to reproduce</summary>

1. Admin suspends the approved household (POST /admin/households/{id}/suspend or UI) - API GET /households/{slug} immediately returns 404
2. Poll the public web pages as an anonymous visitor every 10-13 s for ~110 s

</details>

### Request-more-info has no applicant resubmit step and no signal back to the admin queue (FR-ADM-03)
`s6-03` · P2 · FR-ADM-03 · reproduced 1x

- **Where:** POST /api/v1/admin/households/{id}/request-info; /vi/studio/ho-so
- **Expected:** FR-ADM-03: 'Yeu cau bo sung (ho sua va nop lai)': applicant edits and resubmits, application returns to the queue.
- **Actual:** REQUEST_INFO is PENDING_REVIEW -> PENDING_REVIEW, so the application never leaves the queue and looks identical (same badge 'Dang cho Ban quan ly duyet'); the applicant has no resubmit action and the admin gets no notification or marker that the applicant answered. The old reason stays in statusReason after the edit.
- **Suspected cause:** packages/domain/src/household/household-state-machine.ts:57 (self-transition, no NEEDS_INFO state or resubmit event)

<details><summary>Steps to reproduce</summary>

1. Admin: Yeu cau bo sung with a reason on a pending applicant
2. Applicant: open /vi/studio/ho-so (sees the reason), PATCH /me/household and upload another document
3. Admin: look at the queue

</details>

### Admin dashboard has no trend chart (FR-ADM-06)
`s6-01` · P2 · FR-ADM-06 · reproduced 2x

- **Where:** /vi/admin
- **Expected:** FR-ADM-06: dashboard shows active households, pending applications, open RFQs, in-production orders, QR scans 30 days AND a trend chart.
- **Actual:** Only five static number cards plus the assistant stats card; no chart (0 svg/canvas/figure elements). The API (GET /admin/dashboard) returns only the five scalars, no time series.
- **Suspected cause:** apps/web/src/features/admin/admin-dashboard.tsx renders only METRICS; packages/contracts/src/households/index.ts AdminDashboardSchema has no series

<details><summary>Steps to reproduce</summary>

1. Sign in as admin (aal2)
2. Open /vi/admin and /en/admin
3. Look for a trend/time-series chart next to the five counters

</details>

### Review screen cannot distinguish CCCD / residence proof / workshop photos and does not draw the village boundary (FR-ADM-02)
`s6-04` · P3 · FR-ADM-02 · reproduced 2x

- **Where:** /vi/admin/duyet-ho/{id}
- **Expected:** FR-ADM-02: documents column shows CCCD, residence confirmation and workshop photos; map shows location checked against the village polygon.
- **Actual:** All uploads are one flat list captioned only by mime type (image/png) because the wizard does not ask what each file is (caption null); the map shows only a pin, the boundary check is a text badge 'Ghim ngoai ranh gioi xa Bat Trang' (the polygon is not drawn); the map is aria-hidden. The red warning itself works.
- **Suspected cause:** apps/web/src/features/auth/document-upload.tsx (no document type), apps/web/src/features/admin/workshop-review-map.tsx (no polygon layer)

<details><summary>Steps to reproduce</summary>

1. Open the review screen of a pending applicant with one uploaded paper

</details>

### Audit log shows raw UUIDs as the target instead of a readable name
`s6-09` · P3 · FR-ADM-05 · reproduced 1x

- **Where:** /vi/admin/nhat-ky
- **Expected:** FR-ADM-05 and the screen's own lead text: who, what, when, on which object, before/after values.
- **Actual:** The 'Doi tuong' column shows the entity kind plus a raw UUID (e.g. 'Ho 01a1b585-d5a9-...'), so an admin cannot tell which household or news item was affected without opening it; for news.delete the row is the only trace of the title (kept in the before values).
- **Suspected cause:** apps/web/src/features/admin/audit-log.tsx renders entityId; AuditEntrySchema has no target label

<details><summary>Steps to reproduce</summary>

1. Open the audit log as admin

</details>

### Admin review page overflows horizontally at 1024 px (outside-village badge wider than its card)
`s6-06` · P3 · FR-ADM-02 · reproduced 2x

- **Where:** /vi/admin/duyet-ho/{id}
- **Expected:** Admin UI stays usable at 1024 px without page-level horizontal scroll.
- **Actual:** document.scrollWidth > innerWidth (the three review columns are 232 px each and the badge 'Ghim ngoai ranh gioi xa Bat Trang' is nowrap and sticks out of the card by ~8 px, producing a horizontal scrollbar). Reproduced twice. Dashboard, queue, news list and audit log do not overflow at 1024.
- **Suspected cause:** apps/web/src/features/admin/household-review.tsx: Badge inside the workshops list has no wrapping; grid lg:grid-cols-3 is too narrow at 1024 with the 14rem sidebar

<details><summary>Steps to reproduce</summary>

1. Sign in as admin, set viewport 1024x768
2. Open the review page of an applicant whose workshop pin is outside the Bat Trang polygon

</details>

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Fixed: Suspended household stays publicly visible on household/product/trace pages for 100+ seconds (stale page cache) (`s6-07`)
- [ ] Fixed: Request-more-info has no applicant resubmit step and no signal back to the admin queue (FR-ADM-03) (`s6-03`)
- [ ] Fixed: Admin dashboard has no trend chart (FR-ADM-06) (`s6-01`)
- [ ] Fixed: Review screen cannot distinguish CCCD / residence proof / workshop photos and does not draw the village boundary (FR-ADM-02) (`s6-04`)
- [ ] Fixed: Audit log shows raw UUIDs as the target instead of a readable name (`s6-09`)
- [ ] Fixed: Admin review page overflows horizontally at 1024 px (outside-village badge wider than its card) (`s6-06`)
- [ ] Verified on production in a real browser at 360 px and 1440 px; typecheck, lint and tests pass
design: Implementation decisions: keep household publication statuses unchanged; derive pending reviewState from active statusReason and persisted resubmittedAt, with an explicit owner-only optimistic-concurrency resubmit action and an audited/admin-visible signal. Classify private CERTIFICATE application evidence as IDENTITY, RESIDENCE, WORKSHOP or UNKNOWN via typed document metadata without changing public certificate verification. Admin trend uses persisted TraceScan events for 30 Vietnam calendar days with zero filling and bounded SQL aggregation. Public moderation-sensitive fetches must recheck API on each new server request; unrelated caches stay unchanged. Reuse BAT_TRANG_BOUNDARY. Audit labels use safe event snapshots or authorized household/news lookups, preserving UUID fallback. Local acceptance will be verified; production acceptance requires deployment of this change.

## Problem

Remaining FR-ORD-07..11 and BR-L8 gaps after the main order flow passed end to end.

Found by the end-to-end system test of production (https://vcraft-vn.vercel.app, branch `main`, 2026-11-07) against `docs/SRS.md` and `docs/requirements/vCraft.pdf`. Each item was reproduced at least twice unless noted.

Requirements: `BR-05`, `BR-L8`, `FR-ORD-07`, `FR-ORD-08`, `FR-ORD-09`, `FR-ORD-10`, `FR-ORD-11`, `FR-RFQ-08`, `FR-RFQ-12`, `FR-RFQ-13`

## Findings

### Order progress is not shown as overall % nor as a Gantt chart for buyer/household; at-risk warnings only on the admin progress page
`s5-09` · P2 · FR-ORD-07 · reproduced 2x

- **Where:** /vi/yeu-cau-bao-gia/:id; /vi/studio/don-hang; /vi/admin/tien-do
- **Expected:** FR-ORD-07: the order shows total progress (%), a Gantt chart of allocations and at-risk warnings.
- **Actual:** Buyer sees per-allocation 'x / y cái' lines without household names or a total %. Studio shows only its own card. A Gantt with 'Đúng tiến độ/Chậm/Quá hạn' badges exists only at /admin/tien-do, and its 'Chia lại' button appears only for BEHIND/OVERDUE shares.

<details><summary>Steps to reproduce</summary>

1. Report progress on R1 allocations, open buyer order page, studio page, admin /admin/tien-do

</details>

### Notification gaps: buyer not told when admin confirms delivery on their behalf; reallocation reuses ALLOCATION_PROPOSED
`s5-12` · P3 · BR-L8, FR-ORD-08, FR-ORD-09 · reproduced 2x

- **Where:** rfq.service.ts confirmReceipt / allocation-schedule.service.ts
- **Expected:** Buyer informed when the order is marked DELIVERED by admin; late household informed of the re-split.
- **Actual:** ORDER_RECEIVED went to the households only (recipients: coordinator + households); the buyer got none. Reallocation sends ALLOCATION_PROPOSED to the target households but nothing to the late household.
- **Suspected cause:** rfq.service.ts confirmReceipt recipientIds omits request.buyer.id

<details><summary>Steps to reproduce</summary>

1. Admin confirms receipt on R1 (UI)
2. Compare /me/quotation-notices of buyer, households

</details>

### Non-selected invited households get no notification when another quotation is accepted; invited households see no stepper
`s4-11` · P3 · FR-RFQ-08, FR-RFQ-12 · reproduced 2x

- **Where:** POST /api/v1/rfqs/:id/accept; /vi/studio/*
- **Expected:** FR-RFQ-08: notify everyone; FR-RFQ-12: stepper on every RFQ screen incl. household pages
- **Actual:** Only the chosen household (ALLOCATION_PROPOSED) and the coordinator are notified; others see only RFQ_INVITED. Household invitation list/offer pages have no stepper (Stepper is used only in buyer-rfq-detail.tsx)
- **Suspected cause:** rfq.service.ts acceptQuotation() recipients; no Stepper in apps/web/src/features/rfq/live-contribution-workspace.tsx

<details><summary>Steps to reproduce</summary>

1. 3 households invited, one is in the accepted quotation; list /me/notifications of the other two

</details>

### No buyer rating of households after delivery and no rating in matching
`s5-11` · P3 · FR-ORD-11, BR-05 · reproduced 2x

- **Where:** /vi/yeu-cau-bao-gia/:id (DELIVERED)
- **Expected:** FR-ORD-11 (Could): 1-5 stars + comment after delivery, score used by RFQ matching.
- **Actual:** No UI after DELIVERED (seeded RFQ 111 as well), all probes 404; invitations are chosen by buyer/admin, no scoring.

<details><summary>Steps to reproduce</summary>

1. Deliver R3 and open the page; probe POST /rfqs/:id/review(s)|rating, /reviews

</details>

### Admin cannot create an RFQ on behalf of an off-platform customer
`s5-10` · P3 · FR-ORD-10 · reproduced 2x

- **Where:** POST /api/v1/rfqs
- **Expected:** FR-ORD-10 (Could): admin creates RFQ for a phone customer and coordinates it.
- **Actual:** 403 AUTH_FORBIDDEN (only BUYER role); no admin UI for it.
- **Suspected cause:** rfq.controller.ts:46 @Roles('BUYER')

<details><summary>Steps to reproduce</summary>

1. As demo.admin POST /rfqs with a valid body

</details>

### No way to duplicate an old request into a new draft
`s4-12` · P3 · FR-RFQ-13 · reproduced 2x

- **Where:** /vi/yeu-cau-bao-gia, /vi/yeu-cau-bao-gia/:id
- **Expected:** FR-RFQ-13 (Could): "Nhân bản RFQ cũ thành nháp mới" action
- **Actual:** No duplicate/clone control in the UI and no endpoint in apps/api rfq.controller.ts

<details><summary>Steps to reproduce</summary>

1. Open the buyer list and the detail of a CANCELLED/DELIVERED request

</details>

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Fixed: Order progress is not shown as overall % nor as a Gantt chart for buyer/household; at-risk warnings only on the admin progress page (`s5-09`)
- [ ] Fixed: Notification gaps: buyer not told when admin confirms delivery on their behalf; reallocation reuses ALLOCATION_PROPOSED (`s5-12`)
- [ ] Fixed: Non-selected invited households get no notification when another quotation is accepted; invited households see no stepper (`s4-11`)
- [ ] Fixed: No buyer rating of households after delivery and no rating in matching (`s5-11`)
- [ ] Fixed: Admin cannot create an RFQ on behalf of an off-platform customer (`s5-10`)
- [ ] Fixed: No way to duplicate an old request into a new draft (`s4-12`)

Notification policy conflicts with current SRS FR-RFQ-08/notice table; ratings conflict with simplified BR-05; off-platform customer needs Buyer/Guest ownership and consent decisions. description:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

Imported for mad-uet. Source tracking epic; implement bounded children. Audit evidence is from 2026-11-07 and was not re-reproduced during import. No source comments. Close after all findings and deployed acceptance are resolved.

## Problem

Found by the end-to-end system test of production (https://vcraft-vn.vercel.app, branch `main`, 2026-11-07) against `docs/SRS.md` and `docs/requirements/vCraft.pdf`. Each item was reproduced at least twice unless noted.

Requirements: `FR-AUTH-04`, `FR-AUTH-06`, `FR-AUTH-07`, `NFR-SEC-01`, `NFR-SEC-02`

## Findings

### Cloudflare Turnstile is not active on production sign-up, sign-in and forgot-password forms (no widget, Supabase accepts password grants without a captcha token)
`s0-01` · P2 · FR-AUTH-07 · reproduced 2x

- **Where:** https://vcraft-vn.vercel.app/vi/dang-nhap, /vi/dang-ky, /vi/quen-mat-khau
- **Expected:** FR-AUTH-07 (Should): CAPTCHA (Cloudflare Turnstile) on the sign-up, sign-in and forgot-password forms, enforced by Supabase Auth.
- **Actual:** No Turnstile widget on any of the three pages (0 elements, 0 Cloudflare requests, desktop and mobile). The password grant returns 200 with no captcha_token, so Supabase CAPTCHA protection is also off. ### Password policy is not enforced: Supabase accepts 8-9 character, no-uppercase, no-digit and leaked passwords on password change, and the sign-up form only requires 8 characters with letters and digits
`s3-03` · P2 · NFR-SEC-01 · reproduced 2x

- **Where:** https://vcraft-vn.vercel.app/vi/dang-ky ; PUT {SUPABASE_URL}/auth/v1/user
- **Expected:** NFR-SEC-01: password >= 10 characters with upper case, lower case and a digit, leaked-password protection enabled on Supabase.
- **Actual:** All of those were accepted (HTTP 200). An 8-character 'Ab1xxxxx' also passed length (rejected only as same_password). The sign-up form hint says 'Ít nhất 8 ký tự, gồm cả chữ và số' and client validation only checks 8 chars + letter + digit.
- **Suspected cause:** supabase/config.toml:22-23 itself sets minimum_password_length = 8 and password_requirements = "letters_digits" (and the sign-up form mirrors it); leaked-password protection is not enabled.

title: Fox assistant: thought bubble clipped by the chat panel; render it on the top layer (GH#226)
description:
## Problem
When the chat panel is open, the fox mascot in the panel header shows a thought bubble (`Mascot` `thought` prop, `packages/ui/src/mascot/mascot.tsx`) while Cáo is answering. The bubble sits above the mascot, but the panel container (`assistant-widget.tsx`, `fixed ... z-50 ... overflow-hidden rounded-card`) clips it, so only its bottom edge is visible above the header and the text cannot be read.

## Approach
- Render the thought bubble on the top layer so it overlaps the panel border, the chat and the page behind it: e.g. render it in a portal (or a sibling outside the `overflow-hidden` box) positioned from the mascot's bounding box, with a z-index above the panel (`z-50`) and the page header.
- Keep it anchored to the mascot when the panel moves (map-page lift, resize, scroll) and inside the viewport (flip/shift near the top edge and on small screens).
- Keep it non-interactive (`pointer-events: none`) so it never blocks the chat or the page.
- Same fix for the mobile drawer header if it clips there too.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The whole thought bubble (clouds and text) is visible above the panel, on top of the chat and the page
- [ ] Stays attached to the mascot and inside the viewport on desktop and mobile widths, including the map page
- [ ] Does not block clicks on the panel or the page; readable in light and dark themes
- [ ] Typecheck, lint and tests pass
- [ ] Verified in a real browser (screenshots, no console errors, no 4xx/5xx)

title: Fox assistant: wave typing indicator (three bouncing dots) while Cáo is thinking (GH#225)
description:
## Problem
While Cáo is waiting for an answer, the pending chat bubble only shows the static text "Cáo đang nghĩ…" (`assistant-panel.tsx`, `Bubble`, `message.status === 'pending'`). There is no typing indicator, so the chat feels frozen on slow answers.

## Approach
- Add a wave typing indicator to the pending bubble: three dots that rise and fall one after another, left to right (staggered delay, looping), next to or instead of the text.
- Animate only `transform`/`opacity` (composite-only); keep the brand palette, readable in light and dark themes.
- Keep an accessible label (`aria-live`/visually hidden "Cáo đang nghĩ…") so screen readers still announce the state.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion`, show static dots (or a gentle opacity pulse) instead of the wave.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Pending bubble shows three dots bouncing in a left-to-right wave until the answer starts streaming
- [ ] Screen readers still get the "thinking" state; reduced motion turns the wave off
- [ ] Works in the desktop panel and the mobile drawer, light and dark themes
- [ ] Typecheck, lint and tests pass
- [ ] Verified in a real browser (screenshots, no console errors, no 4xx/5xx)

title: Maps: Google Maps-style pin icons and an info card when tapping a pin (GH#216)
description:
## Problem
The maps are hard to read and give little information when you tap a place:

- **Main map** (`/ban-do`, MapLibre in `apps/web/src/features/village-map/map-canvas.tsx` + `village-map-explorer.tsx`): workshops are drawn as small `circle` layers (7 px glaze/clay dots, ink-black clusters). They look like plain dots, it is not obvious they are tappable, and open vs closed or the kind of place is hard to tell apart. The popup (`pin-popup.tsx`) is plain.
- **Village mini maps** (`village-mini-map.tsx`, used on the home page, in `MapWithList` / `VisitSection` on each artisan page `/nghe-nhan/[slug]` and on the trace page `/truy-xuat/[code]`): pins are small seal marks; tapping a pin shows nothing.

Visitors expect Google Maps-like behaviour: clear pin icons, and a tap shows a card with the basics.

## Approach
- **Pin icons.** Replace the dots with a teardrop/marker pin (SVG image added with `map.addImage` or a `symbol` layer, sized for a 44 px tap target) with an icon inside per workshop purpose (workshop/showroom/kiln…, from `purpose`), coloured by status: open now (glaze), closed (muted clay), production only (ash). Selected pin grows and is raised. Keep the brand palette (BRAND.md) and both light and dark themes readable.
- **Clusters.** Readable count badges in brand colours instead of black blobs; tap zooms in (existing behaviour).
- **Info card on tap (main map).** Google Maps-style card: cover photo, household name, workshop name, craft, open/closed status with the next opening time (`OpenStatus`), address, visiting info, and actions: "View household" and "Directions" (a Google Maps directions link built from lat/lng). On phones show it as a bottom sheet instead of a floating popup; close with ×, Esc or tapping the map.
- **Info card on tap (mini maps).** Pins become buttons; tapping or pressing Enter shows a small card with name, household, address, visitable status and a link (to the household page or the full map centred on that workshop). The adjacent text list stays as the accessible alternative.
- **Legend.** A small legend explaining pin colours/icons on the main map.
- **Accessibility.** Pins and cards keyboard reachable, visible focus, labels for screen readers, reduced motion turns off the pulse/zoom animations.
- **Data.** Use the fields already in `MapPinDto` (`purpose`, `address`, `visitingInfo`, `openingHours`, `household.*`, `lat`/`lng`); no API change unless something essential is missing.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Main map shows marker-style pin icons that differ clearly by status (open / closed / production only), with a legend
- [ ] Tapping a pin on the main map opens an info card (photo, names, craft, status, address, visiting info, "View household", "Directions"); a bottom sheet on mobile
- [ ] Clusters use readable brand-coloured badges
- [ ] Mini maps (home, artisan page, trace page): tapping a pin shows a small info card with a link
- [ ] Works with keyboard and screen readers; reduced motion respected; readable in light and dark themes
- [ ] Unit tests for the new pure logic (icon/status choice, directions URL); typecheck, lint and tests pass
- [ ] Verified in a real browser on desktop and mobile width (screenshots, no console errors, no 4xx/5xx)

title: Home hero: remove the static vase photo and keep only the forming, turning vase animation (GH#215)
description:
## Problem
The home hero (`apps/web/src/app/[locale]/(marketing)/page.tsx`) shows a static museum photo of a vase (`HERO_PHOTO`, id `binh-men-lam-xam`, credit "Ảnh: Daderot · CC0 · Nguồn") as the poster. The 3D vase that forms and turns (`HeroVase` in `apps/web/src/experience/hero-vase/`, GH#94) only fades in over it after the first scroll or 2.5 s after hydration. So visitors first see a stock photo with a photo credit, and then the picture changes under them. We want the hero to show only the forming, turning vase animation.

## Approach
- **Drop the hero photo.** Set `HERO_PHOTO` to `undefined` (or remove it with its `PhotoCredit` line and the related comments). Do not delete the image file or its manifest entry: the same photo is the cover of product BT7K2QXM.
- **Show the animation from the start.** On devices where `canRun3d` passes, start loading the 3D scene right after hydration instead of waiting for a scroll or 2.5 s, and show it as soon as its first frame is ready.
- **Placeholder and fallback.** Until the scene is ready, and on devices where 3D does not run (phones, reduced motion, data saver, no WebGL, low-end hardware), show the hand-drawn `VaseFigure` that the page already renders when there is no hero photo. No empty box, no layout shift.
- **Smooth hand-off.** Cross-fade from `VaseFigure` to the 3D vase; keep the trace seal stamp (`TraceSealFrame`) and the 4/5 frame as they are.
- **Performance.** The LCP element moves from the photo to text/SVG; check that the mobile Lighthouse score does not drop and three.js still stays out of the route's first-load JS.
- **Comments and docs.** Update the comments in `page.tsx` and `hero-vase.tsx` that call the photo the poster/LCP element, and `docs/BRAND.md` §6.3 if it mentions the photo poster.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The home hero no longer shows the museum vase photo or the "Ảnh: Daderot" credit
- [ ] On capable desktops the forming, turning 3D vase appears without needing a scroll and without a 2.5 s wait
- [ ] On phones, reduced motion and other non-3D cases the hand-drawn vase shows instead; no empty frame
- [ ] No layout shift when the 3D scene takes over; the trace seal stamp still sits on the frame
- [ ] Product BT7K2QXM still shows its cover photo
- [ ] Typecheck, lint, tests and e2e pass; mobile Lighthouse score not lower than before
- [ ] Verified in a real browser on desktop and mobile width (screenshots, no console errors, no 4xx/5xx)

title: Theme toggle: wave animation when switching between light and dark (GH#214)
description:
## Problem
Switching between light and dark today is a plain root cross-fade. `applyTheme` in `apps/web/src/components/shell/theme-toggle.tsx` calls `document.startViewTransition`, and `globals.css` runs the shared `kiln-vt-out` / `kiln-vt-in` opacity animation on `::view-transition-old(root)` / `::view-transition-new(root)`. It works, but it feels flat for such a visible control. We want the new theme to spread over the page as a wave that starts at the toggle button.

## Approach
- **Wave reveal.** Keep the View Transitions API. Animate `::view-transition-new(root)` with a `clip-path` that grows from the toggle button's centre until it covers the viewport (radius = distance to the farthest corner). Give the edge a soft wave shape (for example an SVG/`path()` mask or a few layered ripples) so it reads as a wave, not a hard circle. The old snapshot stays still underneath (`animation: none`).
- **Start point.** Pass the click coordinates (or the button's centre for keyboard activation) to CSS through custom properties on `<html>` (for example `--theme-wave-x`, `--theme-wave-y`, `--theme-wave-r`).
- **Scope it to the theme switch only.** The root cross-fade is shared with the sealed sign-in navigation and soft navigations with `<ViewTransition>`. Mark the theme switch (for example `data-theme-transition` on `<html>` while it runs, or `startViewTransition({ types: ['theme'] })` where supported) and override the root animation only for that case, so the other transitions keep the cross-fade.
- **Timing.** Use the motion tokens (`ease.clay`, a duration around `dur.slow`; about 500-700 ms). Clicks during a running transition must not stack or leave the page half-switched.
- **Fallbacks.** No View Transitions API: plain swap (as today). `prefers-reduced-motion`: plain swap or the short cross-fade, no wave.
- **Docs.** Update the comment in `globals.css` and `docs/BRAND.md` if it describes the theme switch as a cross-fade.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Clicking the theme toggle reveals the new theme as a wave spreading from the button and covering the whole viewport
- [ ] Keyboard activation (Enter/Space) starts the wave from the button's centre
- [ ] The sealed sign-in navigation and the product-card morph keep their current transitions
- [ ] Reduced motion and browsers without View Transitions switch without the wave
- [ ] Rapid repeated clicks end in the right theme with no stuck clip or flicker; the sticky header does not jump
- [ ] `apps/web/test/theme-toggle.test.tsx` still passes and covers the new start-point logic; typecheck, lint and tests pass
- [ ] Verified in a real browser (Chrome and Safari, light→dark and dark→light, desktop and mobile width)

title: Fox assistant: bring back the dizzy reaction when clicked many times (GH#211)
description:
## Problem
Clicking the Fox assistant launcher several times in a row used to make the Fox look dizzy. Production no longer does this: every click only opens or closes the panel.

The art is still there:
- the reactions sheet `/mascots/fox-reactions.webp` has a `dizzy` frame (`REACTIONS` in `packages/ui/src/mascot/mascot-model.ts`)
- `MOOD_REACTION` maps the `confused` mood to `dizzy`

Today, though, `apps/web/src/features/assistant/assistant-widget.tsx` sets `confused` only when the last message has `status === 'error'`. The repo history of `packages/ui/src/mascot` has no click-count code. The behaviour probably came from the page-mascot reference component (head follows the pointer, reacts when clicked) and was lost when the Fox moved to the sprite sheets (#140) or in later changes. It is related to #203, which brings back the pointer gaze.

## Approach
- **Count clicks.** Count rapid clicks or taps on the Fox, for example 4 or more within about 1.5 s; tune it so it feels playful, not accidental.
- **Show the dizzy reaction.** When that happens, show `dizzy` for about 1.5-2 s, optionally with a small wobble or spin of the head, then return to the current mood.
- **Lighter feedback.** Single clicks may show a lighter reaction (for example `surprised` or `heart`) before the panel toggles.
- **Where it applies.** It works on the launcher, and on the Fox in the open panel if it is clickable there.
- **Keep the panel usable.** Opening and closing the panel must not break: the dizzy reaction is cosmetic and must not swallow the toggle or trap focus.
- **Where the logic goes.** Put the reusable click-reaction logic in `Mascot` (`packages/ui`), for example an `onPoke` or `reactOnClick` prop or a hook, so other mascots can use it. Cover the counting and timing with unit tests (fake timers).
- **Reduced motion.** With `prefers-reduced-motion`, swap the frame without the wobble animation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Clicking the Fox about 4+ times quickly shows the dizzy face for a moment, then it goes back to normal
- [ ] Normal single clicks still open and close the assistant panel; keyboard (Enter/Space) still works
- [ ] Reduced motion: no wobble, frame swap only
- [ ] Unit tests for the click counter; typecheck, lint and tests pass
- [ ] Verified in a real browser on production (desktop and touch emulation)
