title: Home 'Một ngày ở Bát Tràng': step-by-step stage animation instead of showing all six stages at once (GH#210)
description:
Today the 'Một ngày ở Bát Tràng' section on the home page (apps/web/src/app/[locale]/(marketing)/page.tsx ~line 160, wrapper apps/web/src/experience/motion/day-story.tsx, GH#95) renders all six production stages as one horizontal strip. On desktop it pins and scrubs the strip sideways, but several cards are visible at once, so it reads as a gallery, not a journey. The owner wants a beautiful, smooth animation that walks the viewer through the stages one at a time, from stage 01 to the last, so each transition feels like moving to the next step of a potter's day.

Direction (implementer may refine; run the impeccable / animate guidance before building):
- Pinned scroll story: while the section is pinned, one stage is in focus at a time. Scrolling advances to the next stage with a clear transition (e.g. current photo/text exits, next one enters; crossfade + slight parallax/scale on the 3:4 photo, text lines staggering in).
- A progress indicator showing where the viewer is in the day: step counter '01 / 06' and/or a progress rail with the six stage names, the active one highlighted, past ones marked done. Clicking a step jumps to it.
- Snap to whole stages (no resting half-way between two stages); scrub must feel smooth, no jank. Animate transform/opacity/clip-path only (see the animation-performance skill); keep 60fps on a mid laptop.
- Reuse the existing stack (gsap + ScrollTrigger + Lenis already in day-story.tsx, 'motion' also available); lazy-load as today.
- Content stays the same: DAY_STAGES, stage names/texts from the 'stages' messages, photos from lib/demo/stage-photos.ts.

Constraints:
- prefers-reduced-motion and narrow screens (< 1024px, where useRichMotion is off today): no pinning; show stages one at a time with simple prev/next or a native snap carousel, or the current strip as fallback. Must stay keyboard-operable (WCAG 2.1.1) and screen-reader friendly: all six stages remain in the DOM as an ordered list; the active stage is announced (aria-current or similar), hidden stages are not focus traps.
- Do not regress LCP: keep the server-rendered markup and the note about scroll-smooth + snap causing NO_LCP in Chrome.
- Pinning must not break the sections before/after (no layout jump on refresh/resize, ScrollTrigger refresh on resize).
- Coordinate with vCRAFT-9l8, which removes the PhotoCreditsNote line under this section.,
acceptance_criteria:
- On desktop with motion allowed, scrolling through the section shows exactly one stage in focus at a time, advancing 01 -> 06 in order with a smooth transition, then releases the pin and continues to the next section
- A progress indicator (counter and/or rail) reflects the active stage and lets the viewer jump to a stage
- Reduced motion and mobile get a non-pinned, one-stage-at-a-time or strip fallback that is keyboard and screen-reader operable
- No console errors, no layout jump on resize; Lighthouse performance/LCP on the home page not worse than before
- Verified in a real browser (headless Playwright screenshots/video at desktop and mobile widths, reduced-motion on and off) through the user-facing URL; typecheck, lint and web tests pass

title: Fox mascot: blinking snaps the head back to center and flickers (GH#186)
description:
## Problem
While the fox is looking toward the pointer (e.g. turned left/up-right), every blink snaps its head back to the front-facing pose for ~BLINK_MS, then jumps back to the gaze direction. With the 60 ms opacity cross-fade between two layers it reads as a jerky twitch every 3–6 s. It looks broken.

## Root cause
packages/ui/src/mascot/mascot.tsx (~L195–L260): a blink sets showReaction=true, which hides the directions layer (fox-directions.webp, gaze-driven cell) and shows the reactions layer at the 'blink' cell of fox-reactions.webp. That blink cell is a single front-facing pose, so the gaze direction is lost during the blink. Both layers also cross-fade opacity over 60 ms, which adds the flicker.

## Expected
- The fox keeps facing wherever it is looking (all 9 gaze directions) while it blinks; only the eyes close.
- Blink cadence stays as is: every few seconds (nextBlinkDelay 3–6 s, occasional double blink), none under prefers-reduced-motion.
- No visible flicker/jump between frames during the blink.
- Mood reactions (heart, sparkle, think, refuse, ...) keep their current behaviour.

## Possible approaches (pick in design)
1. Add closed-eye variants for each of the 9 directions (e.g. a fox-directions-blink sheet aligned to the same atlas) and swap only the cell, same layer, no cross-fade.
2. Or overlay per-direction eyelid sprites/shapes on top of the directions layer during the blink instead of switching layers.
In both cases, drop the reactions layer from the blink path.

## Acceptance
- Point the cursor at each of the 9 regions around the fox and wait for blinks: the head never turns to center during a blink.
- No double-layer opacity flash on blink (check in a real browser, frame-by-frame or slowed recording).
- packages/ui/test/mascot.test.tsx covers: blinking does not change the rendered direction cell.
- Reduced motion: still no blinks.
design:
## Recommended fix

Add a third sprite sheet with closed-eye versions of the 9 gaze directions, and make blinking a cell swap on that sheet instead of a switch to the reactions layer.

### 1. New asset: fox-directions-blink.webp
- 1080×1080 WebP with alpha, 3×3 grid of 360×360 px cells, **same row-major order and pixel alignment as fox-directions.webp** (up-left, up, up-right / left, center, right / down-left, down, down-right).
- Each cell is the matching directions cell with only the eyes closed (same closed-eye style as the 'blink' cell in fox-reactions.webp). Head, ears, body and outline must not move by a single pixel.
- Produce it with the page-mascot skill (draw from the existing directions sheet as reference, build the aligned atlas, run its no-jump verification against fox-directions.webp).
- Leave fox-directions.webp and fox-reactions.webp untouched (assets README: do not modify the originals). Put the new file next to them in packages/ui/assets/mascot/ and apps/web/public/mascots/, and document it in the assets README.

### 2. Component (packages/ui/src/mascot/mascot.tsx)
- Add a blink layer stacked directly on top of the directions layer, always mounted (so the sheet is preloaded), using the blink sheet and **the same cellStyle(dirIdx)** as the directions layer.
- Blink only toggles that layer's visibility, with no transition (an instant swap, like a real blink). Remove the 60 ms opacity cross-fade from the blink path.
- showReaction becomes reactionMood !== null only. Blinking no longer touches the reactions layer, and currentReaction no longer depends on blinking.
- When a mood reaction is showing (heart, sparkle, ...), the blink layer stays hidden.
- Keep useBlink / nextBlinkDelay / isDoubleBlink / canBlink as they are (3–6 s cadence, occasional double blink, none under reduced motion).

### 3. Model (packages/ui/src/mascot/mascot-model.ts)
- No new mapping needed: the blink sheet reuses directionIndex. The 'blink' entry in REACTIONS can stay for the sprite index but is no longer used for idle blinking.

### 4. Tests
- mascot.test.tsx: while blinking, the blink layer is visible with the same background-position as the current gaze cell, the directions cell is unchanged, and the reactions layer stays hidden.
- During a mood reaction, blinking does not show the blink layer.
- Reduced motion: no blink layer shown.

### Why this approach
- Fixes both symptoms at the root: the head keeps its direction because the blink frame *is* that direction, and there is no cross-fade between two different poses.
- Stays inside the existing atlas convention (3×3, 300% background-size, 0/50/100% cells), so the code change is small.
- A CSS/SVG eyelid overlay was considered and rejected: it would need hand-tuned eye positions per direction and would not match the hand-drawn sprite style.

title: Plan: SePay checkout with VNPay, MoMo, bank transfer and VietQR
description: Research SePay and existing integrations; write an implementation plan for paying orders via VNPay, MoMo, bank transfer and QR code, fitting the current order/quotation flow.
design:
# Plan: online payment for orders (SePay + VNPay + MoMo)

## Scope decision first
PRODUCT.md lists online payment as out of scope for this version. Changing that needs an ADR (ADR-19 "Online payment for orders") and a PRODUCT.md update. Recommended timing: Release 2, after the defense, running in SANDBOX only until the village administration has a merchant contract and a legal check on collecting money on behalf of households.

## Facts (checked 2026-11-01)
- SePay payment gateway (developer.sepay.vn, official Node SDK `sepay-pg-node`): one-time checkout by signed form POST to `/v1/checkout/init`; payment_method `BANK_TRANSFER` (VietQR), `NAPAS_BANK_TRANSFER` (NAPAS dynamic QR), `CARD` (Visa/Master/JCB 3DS); success/error/cancel URLs; IPN on status change; sandbox env; order API `order.retrieve/all/cancel`.
- SePay does NOT offer VNPay or MoMo. Those need their own direct integrations.
- SePay Webhooks (bank-account webhooks): POST per incoming transfer, must answer 200 `{"success":true}` within 30 s; works with a personal/business bank account linked to SePay; transfer content carries a payment code we generate. Simplest path for "bank" and "QR" on a student budget.
- VNPay: sandbox merchant self-registration (sandbox.vnpayment.vn); maintained TS library `vnpay` (lehuygiang28/vnpay, v2.5, 2026-04). Redirect + IPN, HMAC-SHA512.
- MoMo: test environment with public test credentials (developers.momo.vn); `captureWallet` create → payUrl/deeplink/QR, IPN, HMAC-SHA256. Implement directly (small surface; the npm wrappers are thin and little-used).

## The four methods
| Method | Provider | Flow |
|---|---|---|
| Bank transfer | SePay webhook | Show account, amount, transfer content `VC<code>`; webhook matches content + amount → PAID |
| QR code | SePay (VietQR image from qr.sepay.vn, or PG `NAPAS_BANK_TRANSFER`) | Same reconciliation as bank transfer; QR expires after 15 min |
| VNPay | VNPay direct | Redirect to VNPay, IPN confirms, return URL only shows status |
| MoMo | MoMo direct | payUrl / app deeplink / QR, IPN confirms |
(Card via SePay PG is a free extra once SePay PG is in place.)

## Domain
- What is paid: an **Order** (accepted quotation). Two **Payments** per order: deposit (configurable %, default 30%) before allocations are confirmed / production starts, balance before delivery. Amounts are VND integers fixed at order time.
- New entity `payment`: id, order_id, kind (DEPOSIT|BALANCE), method (BANK_TRANSFER|VIETQR|VNPAY|MOMO), provider (SEPAY|VNPAY|MOMO), amount_vnd, reference_code (unique, goes into transfer content / vnp_TxnRef / orderId), provider_txn_id (unique per provider, nullable), status (PENDING|PAID|FAILED|EXPIRED|CANCELLED|REFUNDED), expires_at, paid_at, raw_last_event (jsonb/json), timestamps. Migration for PostgreSQL and MySQL (integration tests on both).
- Domain state machine in packages/domain (like rfq-state-machine): PENDING→PAID|FAILED|EXPIRED|CANCELLED; PAID→REFUNDED (admin only, manual). Order gains `depositPaidAt`, `balancePaidAt` derived from payments; RFQ/order guards require deposit PAID before production starts.
- Payouts to households stay offline (village administration settles allocations); recorded, not automated.

## Architecture (fits the current NestJS modules + ports)
```text
packages/contracts   zod: CreatePaymentRequest, PaymentView, provider webhook payloads
packages/domain      payment-state-machine.ts, amount/deposit rules
apps/api/src/modules/payments/
  payments.controller.ts     POST /orders/:code/payments (buyer)  GET /payments/:ref (buyer, poll)
  payment-webhooks.controller.ts  POST /payments/webhooks/{sepay,vnpay,momo} (@Public, signature-checked)
  payment-return.controller.ts    GET /payments/return/{vnpay,momo} -> redirect to web status page (never marks PAID)
  payments.service.ts        create, reconcile(event) idempotent, expire
  gateways/ PaymentGateway port { createCheckout(payment) ; verifyWebhook(req) ; queryStatus(ref) }
    sepay.gateway.ts  vnpay.gateway.ts  momo.gateway.ts
apps/worker   job: expire stale PENDING payments; job: query provider status for PENDING older than N min (missed IPN); outbox → notifications (buyer, admin, households)
apps/web      order page: "Pay deposit" → method picker (4 cards) → QR/bank panel with live status (poll GET /payments/:ref every 3 s, stop on final) or redirect for VNPay/MoMo → /[locale]/thanh-toan/[ref] result page
```
Rules: a payment becomes PAID only from a verified webhook/IPN or a server-side status query, never from the browser return URL; amount and reference must match exactly; handle each provider event idempotently (unique provider_txn_id, row lock on payment); respond fast (enqueue heavy work to the outbox); all webhook hits logged with signature result; secrets only on Render (SEPAY_WEBHOOK_API_KEY, SEPAY_MERCHANT_ID/SECRET, VNPAY_TMN_CODE/HASH_SECRET, MOMO_PARTNER_CODE/ACCESS_KEY/SECRET_KEY), never on Vercel. Webhook URLs go through the Vercel rewrite (https://<domain>/api/v1/payments/webhooks/...) — keep-alive cron already prevents Render cold starts.

## Slices (each a PR, test-first)
1. ADR-19 + PRODUCT/GLOSSARY ("Payment / Thanh toán", "Deposit / Đặt cọc").
2. Domain + entity + migration (PG/MySQL) + contracts.
3. SePay bank transfer + VietQR: create, webhook, expiry job, buyer UI with live status. Sandbox/demo mode with a "simulate transfer" admin button gated to APP_ENV!=production.
4. VNPay sandbox (lib `vnpay`): create URL, IPN, return page.
5. MoMo sandbox: create, IPN, return page.
6. Admin: payments list per order, manual mark-refunded, audit log entries; notifications.
7. E2E: Playwright happy path per method using sandbox + signed fake webhooks; docs/deploy.md env table.

## Open questions for the owner
- Deposit % and whether the balance is paid online at all.
- Whose bank account receives money (village administration's) and whether a merchant contract with VNPay/MoMo/SePay PG is realistic; until then sandbox only.
acceptance_criteria: The plan in the design field is reviewed by the team. ADR-19 (online payment) and a PRODUCT.md scope update are written before any code. Implementation is tracked as separate issues (bank transfer/VietQR via SePay webhook, VNPay, MoMo), sandbox only until a merchant contract and legal check exist.

title: Define the deployed demo and release acceptance checks
description:
## Question

What deployed demonstration setup and observable acceptance checks prove that the agreed release works across all required roles and satisfies the original marking criteria?

Use the selected journeys, content direction, and architecture. Decide the hosting and public HTTPS approach, team responsibilities for services, required accounts and representative sample records, and a repeatable demonstration sequence. Include a real-phone QR scan, household approval and publication, workshop discovery, news, quoting, administrator coordination, and progress through delivery. Demonstrate saved data and permitted versus forbidden actions rather than relying on the current local simulations.

Set the evidence needed for database independence, relevant concurrency behavior, responsive and accessible use, upload and display performance, and failure recovery. State how seed/reset operations avoid overwriting the shared development database and what the demonstrator should do if an external service is unavailable. Reconcile the performance and test targets proposed in the SRS with the agreed scope and environment instead of asserting unmeasured results.

The answer should define service choices, sample-data scenarios, an acceptance matrix, and the demonstration conditions. Check for any remaining product or technical decisions and graduate precise ones into new tickets. Do not provision accounts, deploy, seed databases, execute migrations, or build the release in this ticket.
notes: Prerequisite: [Choose the technical architecture and reuse boundaries](vCRAFT-9hg.7). Read the earlier journey and content resolutions to build the acceptance matrix. If this exposes an unresolved decision, create and link the needed question rather than quietly assuming an answer.
close_reason: Demo setup and acceptance checks agreed in grilling, 29 Oct 2026

comments.author: user
comments.text:
## Resolution — human accepted Rounds 1-2, 29 Oct 2026

Grilling type. All twelve questions accepted as recommended.

### Service choices
- Demo runs on one VPS behind Caddy for TLS, with Supabase for auth, Postgres, and Storage. Cloudflare Tunnel plus local build stays as venue-network backup only.
- Mail uses environment SMTP. No provider SDK in the codebase.

### Sample data and accounts
- Fixed demo accounts: one buyer, one household representative, one village administrator, plus one pending household.
- Sample volume: about 20 Bat Trang households, 200 plus products with 4-7 journal stages each, 12 quotation requests across all states, one shared order split across 4 households in production, 15 plus news items.
- One printed QR label on a real ceramic cup. Three pre-logged-in browser profiles for the defense: buyer, household on a real phone, admin.

### Demonstration sequence
- Single repeatable script on the deployed URL: real-phone QR scan, household approval and publication, workshop discovery with map plus text list, news, quoting, admin coordination, allocation confirmations, quantity progress through delivery and receipt.
- Shows saved data and permitted versus forbidden actions live, not local simulations.

### Acceptance matrix
- One row per journey step: step, what the examiner sees on screen, performing role. Covers guest QR scan, buyer quoting, household approval and publishing, admin coordination, delivery progress.

### Evidence checks (all run before exam day on frozen data)
- Lighthouse 90 plus on key pages, zero full reloads in the script, capped image variants with lazy loading, WCAG 2.2 AA.
- Responsive pass at 360, 768, 1440. Keyboard-only QR-to-household path. Text list beside the map counts as the accessible alternative.
- Upload one 12 MB phone photo, confirm it lands near 1.5 MB after client compression. Confirm list pages load the small variant with lazy loading in DevTools network.
- Concurrency: two-tab accept or confirm race on the deployed URL; the stale write is refused with a visible error. No load test.
- Database independence: passing CI matrix run on Postgres and MySQL. No mid-defense database switch.
- Recovery: documented demo database backup before exam day plus one practiced restore to a scratch database. No live restore during the defense.

### Safety and fallback
- `pnpm demo:reset` runs only against the demo database URL, refuses development or production targets, restores the exact accounts and records above.
- If an external service is down in the venue: show the local build with the tunnel first, then state the outage plainly and continue with screenshots of the affected step. No improvised flow.

### Reconciled targets
- SRS performance and test targets from NFR-PERF and NFR-UX stand as pre-exam checks on frozen demo data, not live venue guarantees.

No new decision tickets. No fog graduated. Map scope unchanged.

title: Choose the technical architecture and reuse boundaries
description:
## Question

Which parts of the installed stack, current implementation, and proposed architecture should the first release keep, simplify, replace, or defer to deliver the agreed journeys?

Start with the existing pnpm/Turborepo workspace, Next.js and React frontend, NestJS/Fastify API, MikroORM database layer, Supabase services, Redis/BullMQ proposal, shared contracts and domain packages, and UI/i18n assets. Distinguish an installed dependency from an implemented integration. Compare alternatives only where a requirement, operational burden, or demonstrated constraint gives a concrete reason.

Resolve authoritative storage and authentication boundaries, API and shared-contract ownership, transactions and concurrency for quotations, media processing and access, notifications needed by the retained workflows, and the database independence required by the course. Address how the frontend hash-chain code and existing pure domain rules should be reused. Account for map, editor, animation, and AI dependencies according to the decisions that retained or excluded them.

Read ADRs 13-15 and the architecture decision summary. Record any accepted reversal explicitly; do not silently override Supabase choices or the MySQL portability obligation. If a decision depends on facts outside the repository, create a focused research ticket and leave that part unresolved until evidence arrives. The answer should specify responsibilities, reuse boundaries, and justified trade-offs with no implementation or migration execution.
notes: Prerequisites: [Define quotation and shared-order coordination rules](vCRAFT-9hg.5) and [Choose the exhibition journey, content, and visual direction](vCRAFT-9hg.6). Together with their prerequisite resolutions, these establish the behavior the architecture must support. The installed stack is a starting point, not a requirement to use every dependency.
close_reason: Human accepted Q1-Q18; resolution recorded

comments.author: user
comments.text:
## Resolution

The human accepted Q1-Q18 through three grilling rounds. No reversals of ADRs 13-15. No research tickets needed: every decision rested on repo facts or prior resolutions.

### Kept as specified (no change)

- ADRs 13, 14, 15 stand. Supabase keeps Auth, Storage over S3, business Postgres, and pgvector. Browser talks to Supabase directly only for sign in, refresh, and MFA. All business data goes through the API. No Data API access touches business tables. MySQL portability stays a tested obligation: dual-driver entities and migrations, CI integration tests on MySQL via Testcontainers, compose mysql profile for local checks. Postgres-only SQL lives only in supabase migrations.
- Contracts own the API boundary. Zod schemas validate both sides and generate the OpenAPI document. Controllers stay thin: map entities to DTOs, hold no business logic.
- Optimistic versioning for acceptance races. Accept-bid and confirm-allocation run in one transaction checking a version column; stale writes are refused. No pessimistic locks at demo scale.
- Deployment is one VPS plus Supabase. Caddy terminates TLS and routes same-origin traffic. VPS runs web, api, worker, Redis. Supabase hosts Auth, Postgres, Storage. Local storage driver is the offline demo fallback only.
- Package boundaries are enforced in CI via dependency-cruiser per ARCHITECTURE 3.2. Domain stays free of framework, ORM, and workspace imports. Web never imports database or api code. UI knows no business logic.
- API conventions stay as specified: /api/v1, cursor pagination, RFC 9457 problems, ETag on public reads, version-checked writes, idempotency keys on state-changing POSTs.
- Mail is an environment detail. SMTP settings come from the environment behind a mail port. Mailpit for dev, VPS SMTP for demo. No provider SDK in the codebase.

### Kept with narrowed scope

- Redis, BullMQ, and the worker stay, scoped to three jobs: media processing, mail delivery, outbox relay. Redis holds no durable data and runs locally on the VPS. The API never does image conversion, PDF rendering, or SMTP sends inline. SSE hub and Redis pub/sub wiring leave the release.
- Live updates use polling. TanStack Query refetch covers offer arrival, allocation confirmation, and progress reports. SSE is deferred.
- Media pipeline runs in the worker with sharp. API validates magic bytes, size, MIME at the boundary. Worker converts to AVIF/WebP, renders QR label PDFs, stores per ADR-14 bucket rules.
- MapLibre stays because the journey decision retained the real map with a text-list companion. R3F hero, GSAP scroll story, and Motion transitions leave the release.
- Hash chain code reused as is. Domain chain logic and the frontend verification copy stay where they are. Backend verifies on journal write, browser re-verifies on public display.
- Notifications are in-app plus email only. Quotation events write an in-app row and queue SMTP mail. No SMS, push, or digest.
- Auth boundary stays as drawn. Supabase owns identity, sessions, refresh, MFA, OAuth. API verifies JWTs via JWKS, enforces RBAC plus resource policies, requires MFA for admin, checks lockout per request. No local passwords.

### Removed from the release

- Assistant stack: no assistant module, no Claude API calls, no Voyage embeddings at runtime. ADR-13 migrations stay so the knowledge table and RPC exist, but nothing reads or writes them.
- TipTap: admin news is plain text with server-side sanitization. Editor dependencies leave the web app.
- Weather: Open-Meteo integration dropped. Nothing retained needs it.

### Out of scope (confirmed, not decided away here)

- Automatic allocation strategies, Gantt, predicted lateness (already excluded by 9hg.5).
- 3D/scroll storytelling, fox assistant, bilingual authoring (already deferred by 9hg.1).

title: Choose the exhibition journey, content, and visual direction
description:
## Question

What public journey and visual treatment make the agreed digital exhibition understandable and distinctive, using content the team can actually supply?

Use the prototype skill to produce only a cheap local artifact for live human feedback. Start from the existing brand tokens, moodboard, maker pages, and production timeline. Compare entering through the home page with scanning a product QR code. Establish the order and hierarchy of household history, maker attribution, objects, process evidence, workshop location and visiting information, and the next step into a wholesale inquiry. Account for the public news and discovery journeys without making a product-price grid the organizing idea by default.

Choose the content forms, realistic sample narrative depth, photography or illustration sources, rights and credits, and clear treatment of fictional sample households. Decide which parts of the current visual direction and animation to retain or simplify within the release boundary. Include mobile reading, accessible navigation, reduced motion, and an accessible alternative to the map. The answer requires human reaction to the artifact and should record the selected journey and visual principles. Link the prototype as an asset; do not build the production UI or claim the design is approved before that exchange.
notes: Prerequisite: [Define production journals and traceability guarantees](vCRAFT-9hg.4). Read its resolution and the prior scope, identity, and approval decisions before preparing the prototype. This question can run alongside [Define quotation and shared-order coordination rules](vCRAFT-9hg.5); do not invent unresolved quotation details in the public prototype.
close_reason: Human reaction recorded; journey selected (A base + C for guests). Resolution comment holds the decisions.

comments.author: user
comments.text:
## Resolution

Prototype asset: docs/design/prototype-exhibition-journey.html. Open it directly in a browser, no server and no build. The bottom bar and the arrow keys switch variants. This is a throwaway artifact for a live reaction, not a production screen, and it is not an approved design.

### What the three variants compare

All three use the same sample, household Gom Minh Hai and the unique vase BT7K2QXM, and the same brand tokens from docs/BRAND.md. They differ in structure, not colour.

- Variant A, Cuon so nghe. One continuous vertical reading: household history, then makers, then the object, then the journal, then visiting, then the wholesale step. This is the home-page entry.
- Variant B, Nam gian phong. The same content split into five rooms reached by a sticky navigation: house, people, object, proof, visit. This tests whether the hierarchy should be browsable rather than sequential.
- Variant C, Quet ma mo so. The QR scan entry. It opens on the seal and the journal, newest stage first, then walks back to the household and the visiting place, with a secondary link to the home page.

### Shared content and trust rules shown in every variant

- Order tested: household history, maker attribution, the object, process evidence, workshop location and visiting information, then one step into a wholesale inquiry. Public news and discovery sit after that and are organised by household, not by a price grid. No retail price appears on a public page.
- Maker credit names Binh for shaping and Lan for painting. The person who posts is described as household administration and is not credited as a maker.
- The journal uses the seven fixed stages, shows a declared date per stage, shows one public correction with its reason kept beside the original, and carries the single integrity sentence: the sealed account cannot be silently rewritten, and that says nothing about whether the events happened as written.
- Visiting separates a showroom that welcomes visitors from production workshops that do not. The map always has a plain-text list beside it, so the list is the accessible alternative and the map is optional illustration.
- The household is labelled as fictional sample data. Image slots state the rule: real photography needs a clear licence plus a credit line, and sample people are marked as illustration.
- Motion is held to the seal moment plus short transitions, and the page respects reduced motion. The 3D hero and scroll storytelling stay out, matching the release boundary.

### What this ticket still needs

The human has to react to the artifact before a journey and a visual principle can be selected. The six questions at the bottom of the file are the reaction prompts. Until that reaction is recorded, this ticket stays open and no design is treated as chosen.

title: Define quotation and shared-order coordination rules
description:
## Question

What complete quotation and shared-order journeys must the Buyer, Artisan, and village Admin be able to carry out, and which rules determine valid progress?

Reconcile the assignment, the detailed SRS, and the implemented RFQ, Bid, and Allocation state machines. Work through both a single-household quote and the assignment example of 5,000 custom cups shared among households. Decide how invitations and capacity work, how quotations stay private, when offers may change or expire, how acceptance creates an order, and how households confirm and report their allocated work through delivery.

Resolve necessary exception behavior, including concurrent acceptance, a household declining an allocation, inadequate capacity, cancellation, and reassignment, at the level required by the agreed release scope. Determine which proposed allocation strategies and progress displays are justified. Keep payment and shipping integrations outside the boundary. The answer should establish states, invariants, responsibilities, and concrete scenarios; it should not implement controllers or extend the existing machines without a decision.
notes: Prerequisite: [Define approval, publishing, and access rules](vCRAFT-9hg.3). Read its resolution and the linked scope and identity decisions before working this question.
close_reason: Quotation, coordination, privacy, lifecycle and failure rules agreed through Q1-Q13; resolution and source handoff recorded

comments.author: user
comments.text: Discussion checkpoint: the human accepted Q1 and Q2. Each quotation request ends in at most one accepted offer covering its full requested quantity. A household may offer the whole quantity; a household that can supply only part contributes through a cooperative offer assembled by the assigned village administrator. The buyer compares complete offers and does not independently accept fragments of competing offers. The buyer explicitly invites one or several approved households. A separate opt-in shares the request with the assigned administrator for village coordination; that administrator may invite additional households to contribute. There is no automatic broadcast to all households. Existing private-audience rules and the scope deferral of reassignment remain in force. This ticket remains in progress; lifecycle, capacity, pricing, acceptance, allocation confirmation, progress, and exception rules still need live discussion.

comments.author: user
comments.text: Discussion checkpoint: the human accepted Q3 and Q4. Before sending, a request requires the actual design/customisation, quantity, delivery destination, required delivery date, and one quotation deadline. A product page may be a design reference; optional notes and images explain the work. Requested terms are fixed after sending. A material change requires cancelling and replacing the request so households never quote against different specifications. The quotation deadline governs both submission and acceptance and is separate from required delivery. A current quotation is available until the deadline unless its author withdraws or replaces it. Before acceptance the author may submit a revision; private history retains prior versions. Acceptance must name the current version and refuses a stale version after a price change. An unaccepted request expires at the deadline. Acceptance fixes the accepted terms and closes competing offers. The ticket remains in progress pending household commitments, capacity, allocation confirmation, progress/delivery, and exception rules.

comments.author: user
comments.text: Discussion checkpoint: the human accepted Q5-Q7. Each invited household declares its maximum quantity for this request, own unit price, and promised completion date. These declarations do not reserve capacity across other requests. Admin may compose an offer only within each households declared quantity, price, and date, and cannot rewrite its contribution. Buyer acceptance creates one order awaiting exact allocation confirmations; every household confirms or declines its allocation, and no production starts until all confirm. A direct order uses the same sequence with one household. First-release division is manual using a household/quantity/price/completion-date table; sending requires exact full-quantity coverage, each share within its contribution limit, and all dates meeting required delivery. The three proposed automatic allocation strategies are excluded from this release. Contributions are distinct from complete buyer-facing quotations: internal contribution prices are private to the contributing household and administration. The buyer sees participating households, shares, completion dates and one complete cooperative price. Agreed prices use VND. Quotes state production total and any additional charge, or explicitly say delivery is arranged and paid separately. Payments and shipping remain external. Decline, cancellation, progress, receipt and remaining exception rules are still pending.

comments.author: user
comments.text: Discussion checkpoint: the human accepted Q8-Q10. A household declining a proposed allocation cancels the whole unstarted order, preserves quotation/allocation history, and notifies participants; no silent substitution. Before production the buyer or an administrator can cancel the whole order with a required reason. A confirmed household requests administrator cancellation rather than silently withdrawing. Inadequate capacity prevents sending a cooperative quote; the request stays open until deadline or buyer cancellation. The sole household starts a direct order; the assigned admin starts a cooperative order after all allocations confirm. Each representative reports completed quantity bounded from zero to allocated quantity, optional notes/photos, and corrections retaining the earlier report with a required reason. Buyer/admin see household progress and a quantity-weighted overall percentage. A table shows promised dates and flags overdue unfinished shares. Gantt and predicted-lateness displays are excluded. Allocation DONE requires full quantity complete; all DONE permits buyer receipt confirmation or administrator proxy receipt with a written explanation. Production completion never implies delivery. Progress is private and does not automatically create/publish production journals. After production starts only an administrator may cancel an unfulfillable whole order with a required reason; completed quantities/history remain, unfinished allocations cancel, and the order is CANCELLED, never DELIVERED. Lateness alone keeps IN_PRODUCTION with an overdue warning. Accepted terms never change silently. Replacement work needs a new request. Refunds, compensation and disposition of finished goods remain external. Final questions about contribution freshness, eligibility and date boundaries remain open.

comments.author: user
comments.text:
## Resolution

The human accepted Q1-Q13 and confirmed this shared first-release specification. GLOSSARY.md records the vocabulary.

### Requests and offers

- A verified buyer invites selected approved households, requests village coordination, or does both. Coordination alone is valid. One assigned administrator may invite more households. No automatic broadcast, ranked matching or automatic coordination escalation.
- Require design/customisation, positive whole-number quantity, unit, destination, required delivery and quotation deadline. Notes/images are optional. All shares use the same unit. Referencing a product does not reserve or redefine its batch or stock.
- The quotation deadline is any future time, without a 24-hour minimum. Required delivery follows it. Offered completion dates fall after that deadline and on or before required delivery.
- Drafts are editable. Sent specifications and dates are fixed; changes require cancellation and a replacement request using the old details.
- Submission, revision, withdrawal and acceptance require now strictly before the same deadline. Every unaccepted request expires then, with or without offers. There is no seven-day acceptance extension, even if expiry processing runs late.
- The buyer accepts one current, complete quotation covering the full quantity. Revisions retain private history. Stale versions cannot be accepted. Acceptance fixes terms, creates one order and proposed allocations, and rejects competing active quotations.

### Coordination, capacity and privacy

- A household contribution offer states its own maximum quantity for this request, unit price and completion date. Partial contributions go to the administration, not into independently accepted buyer orders. Declared availability does not reserve capacity across requests; no global scheduling or double-booking guarantee is promised.
- The administrator plans manually using households, quantities, prices and dates. Sending requires exact full coverage, positive integer shares within household offers, unchanged household rates, and valid dates. Inadequate capacity prevents sending; the request stays open until cancellation or deadline.
- Changing or withdrawing an input contribution withdraws any dependent unaccepted cooperative quotation and notifies buyer/coordinator. The administrator must check current inputs and issue a new version. Accepted contributions and plans cannot change silently.
- Prices use VND. State production total and additional charges, or explicitly state that delivery is arranged and paid separately. Payments, shipping integrations, refunds, compensation and handling finished goods remain external.
- The buyer sees all complete quotations on their request. A cooperative quotation shows participants, quantities, completion dates and full buyer price. Internal contribution prices are private to the contributing household and administration. Contributions are distinct from complete quotations.
- Representatives see only their own invitations, quotations, contribution history, allocation and progress. Buyers/admins see household and total order progress. Quotation content never reaches guests, public pages, QR pages, search or an assistant. Notifications respect those audiences. Earlier administrative access rules remain.
- Recheck every supplying household at acceptance: approved, not suspended, representative not locked. Acting accounts must also be permitted. After acceptance suspension still permits existing private confirmation/progress; locking prevents representative actions. Production cannot start with a locked participating representative. Wait for unlock or cancel; administrators cannot fabricate household actions.

### Confirmation, production and exceptions

- Acceptance means awaiting household confirmation. Direct orders have one proposed allocation; cooperative orders have their fixed shares. All must confirm before production. The sole household starts a direct order; the assigned administrator starts a cooperative order.
- Declining a proposed allocation cancels the whole unstarted order, preserves the decline and accepted plan, cancels other unfinished shares and notifies participants. There is no substitution or household reassignment. Invitation refusal or no response before acceptance does not cancel a request.
- Before production the buyer or an administrator can cancel the whole request/order with a reason. Discarding an unsent draft retains the no-reason exception. A confirmed household asks for administrator cancellation rather than silently withdrawing.
- Representatives report completed quantity between zero and allocated quantity, with optional notes/photos. Corrections retain the earlier report and require a reason. Allocation completion requires full quantity. Reports stay private and do not automatically create products or publish production journals.
- Show a progress table, household dates and total completed units divided by order quantity. Flag unfinished shares after their promised dates. Omit automatic allocation strategies, Gantt charts and predicted-lateness displays.
- All allocations done means awaiting receipt, not delivered. The buyer confirms receipt, or an administrator records it on behalf of the buyer with a written explanation.
- After production starts, only an administrator can cancel an unfulfillable whole order with a reason. Keep completed quantities, finished allocations and history; cancel unfinished allocations. The order ends cancelled, never delivered. Lateness alone keeps production active with an overdue warning. Replacement work needs a new request.

### States and invariants

Retain RFQ/order states DRAFT, SENT, BIDDING, ACCEPTED, IN_PRODUCTION, DELIVERED, CANCELLED and EXPIRED. The first complete quotation opens BIDDING; contribution offers alone do not. ACCEPTED displays awaiting confirmations. All allocations done derives awaiting receipt without another required persisted state.

Retain quotation states SUBMITTED, ACCEPTED, REJECTED, WITHDRAWN and LAPSED, with version history. Expiry/cancellation lapses open offers; an accepted quotation stays as evidence if its order cancels. Retain allocation states PROPOSED, CONFIRMED, DECLINED, IN_PROGRESS, DONE and CANCELLED, with the whole-order consequences above.

A request yields at most one accepted quotation and one order. Acceptance atomically checks authorization, deadline, current quotation/contribution versions, full quantity, dates, prices and eligibility. Competing acceptances yield one winner. Retries never duplicate orders, allocations or progress events. A racing contribution change either invalidates an offer first or cannot alter an accepted plan. Cancellation, confirmation, start and receipt also check fresh states; no late update may affect a cancelled order. Architecture chooses transaction and retry mechanisms.

### Concrete scenarios

1. Direct: 300 cups at 35,000 VND total 10,500,000 VND. Accept before deadline, confirm the allocation, then start. Reporting 120 cups shows 40 percent. All 300 complete still requires receipt confirmation.
2. Cooperative: 5,000 logo cups within one month. Private contributions of 2,000 at 30,000 VND, 1,500 at 32,000 VND and 1,500 at 34,000 VND total 159,000,000 VND. The buyer sees shares/dates/total, not internal rates. All confirm before administrator start. Reports of 1,000, 600 and 400 cups show 40 percent overall.
3. Contributions totalling 4,800 cannot produce a 5,000-cup offer. Withdrawing an input makes its cooperative offer unavailable. An allocation decline cancels the whole unstarted order. Concurrent acceptance creates one order. Acceptance at the deadline fails even before expiry processing.

title: Define production journals and traceability guarantees
description:
## Question

What does a production journal record, what can a visitor learn or verify through its QR page, and what rules preserve that promise?

Use the agreed object or batch identity and approval rules. Decide how an artisan records stages, timestamps, notes, and images; whether stages can repeat or be missing; what may be published before completion; and how mistakes are corrected. Specify the distinction between an informal household story and evidence tied to an identified product. Cover invalid codes, incomplete journals, unpublished or withdrawn products, changed images, and locked households.

The current web app computes a real hash chain over sample entries, but persistence and authoritative verification are unbuilt. Decide whether the proposed append-only chain belongs in this release, what changes it detects, what it cannot prove, and how the UI states those limits without claiming that a hash proves who physically made an object. Resolve the QR-link and publication lifecycle as product behavior. The answer should provide the journal rules and visitor-facing trust contract, not a hashing implementation.
notes: Prerequisite: [Define approval, publishing, and access rules](vCRAFT-9hg.3). Read its resolution and the linked scope and identity decisions before working this question.
close_reason: Resolved in live discussion on 29 Oct 2026: journal rules and visitor trust contract recorded in the resolution comment.

comments.author: user
comments.text:
## Resolution
The human accepted the recommendations in Q1 through Q7 during the live discussion on 29 October 2026. Q5 was restated by Q7 after a conflict with the approval resolution surfaced. These decisions define the journal rules and the visitor-facing trust contract for the first release. Canonical vocabulary is recorded in root GLOSSARY.md.
### What a journal records
- A production journal belongs to exactly one product, which identifies one object or one production batch. The journal is evidence of the published account of making that product. The household profile and artisan stories are informal narrative and carry no integrity claim.
- A journal entry records one stage, the date the household declares the work happened, a note, and optional images. The system also records when the entry was saved. The QR page shows the declared date as the story date and uses the system time for ordering and correction history. Backdated and future declared dates are allowed and shown exactly as declared.
- The stage vocabulary is the fixed set of seven ceramic stages: clay, throw, dry, paint, glaze, fire, finish. A stage may repeat and a stage may be skipped, but a skipped stage requires one line of reason in its entry. There are no free-text stages in the first release.
### Corrections and integrity
- Before first publication the representative edits entries freely. After publication no entry is edited or deleted silently. A mistake is fixed by a correction entry that names the entry it supersedes, and the QR page shows the original and the correction together.
- An image changed after publication follows the same rule. The old image hash stays in the published history and the replacement arrives as a correction entry.
- The first release keeps the existing SHA-256 append-only hash chain. It detects a change, deletion, or reordering of published entries. It does not prove the events happened as written and it does not prove who physically made the object. The QR page states this in one fixed sentence beside the seal, using the term Journal integrity. A broken chain names the entry that failed and links to it.
### Publication and failure behavior
- A journal is never public on its own. It appears only with its published product and is withdrawn with that product.
- An unfinished journal may be published. The QR page labels it in progress and names the stages not yet recorded.
- An invalid code, an unpublished product, a withdrawn product, and a suspended household all return the same missing page as a bad link.
- Locking the representative account freezes the household's journals. Published pages stay visible, and no new entries or corrections can be added until the lock clears. Locking hides nothing and is not a suspension.
### Follow-through within the existing map
- Choose the exhibition journey, content, and visual direction decides how the journal timeline, the in-progress label, the correction display, and the integrity sentence are presented.
- Choose the technical architecture and reuse boundaries translates these rules into persistence and verification contracts. This ticket does not prescribe a hashing implementation.
No new decision ticket is needed from this resolution. The map's unshaped questions and out-of-scope boundaries are unchanged.

title: Define approval, publishing, and access rules
description:
## Question

Who may create, approve, publish, change, and view each kind of content or record in the first release, and what must each approval claim mean?

Define complete account and household onboarding journeys for Guest, Buyer, Artisan, and village Admin using the agreed domain model. Cover household review and requests for corrections, household stories, workshop information, products, certificates, production journals, public versus household-only news, and access to private quotation data. Separate household approval, certificate verification, journal integrity, and claims of physical authenticity in the public language.

Use representative sample verification documents for the course demo. Decide what rejection, suspension, and unpublishing do to public profiles, existing QR links, private records, and retained workflows. Keep permissions consistent with the original assignment and retained scope, and identify who can act for a household without inventing public social participation. The answer should define the actor/resource/state rules and necessary failure behavior; it should not implement authentication or policies.
notes: Prerequisites: [Set the first-release scope and demonstration priorities](vCRAFT-9hg.1) and [Define the household, maker, workshop, and product model](vCRAFT-9hg.2). Read their resolution comments before working this question.
close_reason: Actor, claim, audience, and failure rules agreed

comments.author: user
comments.text:
Discussion checkpoint: the human accepted Q1 through Q6.

Q1. Four claims stay separate. Household approval is the only gate into the public exhibition and into quoting. Certificate verification covers one declared certificate and is not product authentication. Journal integrity means the household's account was not silently rewritten, not that the events happened as written. The exhibition never says approval, a verified certificate, or a QR code proves the object in hand was made by the household. The course review packet is labeled sample data: declared name, craft, workshop location, workshop photos, and a fictional village confirmation. No national identity documents.

Q2. One account holds one role. A guest sees published public pages. A buyer acts only on their own quotation records. One household representative acts for one household and is not made a maker by doing so. A named artisan without that account cannot act. A village administrator is sample data, not a public signup, and is not a household member. Applying and accepting an invite both wait for the same approval. Someone who buys and represents a household uses two accounts.

Q3. Review states are pending review, needs information, approved, and rejected. Needs information and a later reapplication return the same household record to pending review. Nothing is public before approval. Approval is one decision for the whole household, not a separate decision per page.

Q4. Profile, stories, workshops, certificates, and products appear only while the household is approved. A certificate also needs verification. A journal appears only with its published product and is withdrawn with that product. Household-only news is visible to representatives of approved households and to administrators. For anyone else, including a direct link, it is treated as not existing.

Q5. Rejection keeps the application private. Suspension hides the public profile, products, and workshops. Existing QR codes and saved links show an unavailable notice, not the story and not a missing page. Private quotation records stay visible to their owners and to administrators. While suspended, the representative cannot publish, edit public pages, or place a new bid. Withdrawing one product hides that product and its journal only. Ending suspension restores the hidden pages without a new review, unless the administration separately requires one.

Q6. A buyer sees their own requests and every bid on them. A household sees its own invitations, bids, and share of coordinated work, never another household's prices. Administrators see all quotation records for coordination. Guests see none. No quotation content reaches public pages, search, or the assistant. Asking for village coordination shares the request with the assigned administrator only.

These terms are now in root GLOSSARY.md: Guest, Buyer, Village administration, Village administrator, Household approval, Certificate verification, Journal integrity, Suspension, Household-only news. The ticket remains in progress. Who may create and change each record, what a refused view returns, workshop closure versus suspension, and the public wording of the four claims are still open.

comments.author: user
comments.text:
## Resolution

The human accepted the recommendations in Q1 through Q9 during the live discussion. These decisions define who may act, what each approval claims, and what each audience sees in the first release. Canonical vocabulary is recorded in root GLOSSARY.md.

### Actors and accounts

- One account holds one role. A person who both buys and represents a household uses two accounts. The demo does not switch roles inside one session.
- A guest has no account and sees only published public pages.
- A buyer registers, verifies their email, and then acts only on their own quotation records.
- One household representative account acts for exactly one household. The representative may or may not be a maker. Acting never makes the representative a maker, and a named artisan without this account cannot act.
- A village administrator account is created as sample data, not by public signup. An administrator is not a member of any household and is not credited as a maker for editing or approving something.
- A household enters review in two ways, and both land in the same queue. The representative applies, or an administrator invites the representative. The invite creates the account only. It never approves the household.

### What each approval claims

Four claims stay separate in the public language.

- Household approval means the village administration accepts the household as a craft-producing unit presented in the exhibition. It is the only gate into the public exhibition and into quotation participation. It does not mean every public sentence is true, and it does not mean a named artisan made any particular object.
- Certificate verification means an administrator reviewed one certificate the household declared. An unverified certificate never appears, even on an approved profile. A verified certificate is shown as reviewed, not as proof that a product is genuine.
- Journal integrity means the household's published account of making a product was not silently replaced. It does not mean the events happened as written. How edits are recorded belongs to Define production journals and traceability guarantees.
- Physical authenticity is never claimed. Approval, a verified certificate, and a QR code do not prove that the object in someone's hand was made by this household. The QR code opens the published account of that product.

The course review packet is sample data, clearly labeled as such: the household's declared name, craft, and workshop location, workshop photos, and a fictional village confirmation. It includes no national identity documents or real identity numbers. Approving that packet means accepted into the exhibition.

### Review states

A household application is pending review, needs information, approved, or rejected.

- Nothing is public before approval. Pending review, needs information, and rejected keep the household and its documents private to the household and the administration.
- Needs information means the administration named what is missing. The household edits and resubmits, which returns the same record to pending review.
- Rejected means the administration declined the application with a written reason. The household can correct and reapply, which opens a new review of the same household record.
- Approved is one decision on the whole household, not a separate decision per page. It opens the public profile and quotation participation together.

### Who authors, and who only gates

- The representative authors their own household's story, workshops, products, journals, and certificate declarations. Drafts stay private until published.
- The administration never rewrites a household's story, journal, or bid. It approves the household, marks individual certificates verified, suspends or restores the public presence, and publishes village news. It also authors cooperative bids and coordination plans.
- The buyer authors only their own quotation requests.
- Locking an account stops that account from acting at all, including on private drafts. It does not delete or publish anything, and it is not a suspension.

### What each audience sees

- The household profile, its stories, its workshops, its certificates, and its products appear only while the household is approved.
- A production journal appears only with its published product and is withdrawn with that product.
- Public news shows to everyone. Household-only news shows to representatives of approved households and to administrators. For a guest, a buyer, or anyone else, a direct link is treated as not existing.
- A buyer sees their own requests and every bid on them. A household sees only its own invitations, its own bids and their history, and its own share of coordinated work. One household never sees another household's prices. An administrator sees all quotation records because coordination needs them. A guest sees none.
- No quotation content appears on public pages, in public search, or in the assistant's answers. A buyer who asks for village-level coordination shares that request with the assigned administrator only, and that consent covers coordination, not publication.

### Failure behavior

- When the audience rule is about secrecy, the product hides existence. A guest or buyer opening household-only news, a private draft, or another household's bid gets the same missing page as a bad link. A representative opening the review queue, coordination screens, or another household's records gets the same missing page.
- When the rule is about permission, the product refuses with a reason. Editing another household's product or bidding after the deadline returns 403, and the screen explains the rule in plain words.
- Rejection changes nothing public, because nothing public existed.
- Suspension hides the public profile, all products, and all workshops from listings, the map, and search. Existing QR codes and saved links stay scannable and open a short unavailable notice. They do not show the old story, and they do not pretend the address was always empty. Private quotation drafts and history stay visible to their owners and to administrators. While suspended, the representative cannot publish, edit public pages, or place a new bid. Ending suspension restores what was hidden without a new review, unless the administration separately requires one.
- Withdrawing one product hides that product and its journal, and its QR code opens the same unavailable notice. The rest of the household stays public.
- A workshop's own temporarily-closed flag marks only that workshop. The pin shows closed, the page states the reason and when it may reopen, and the household and its products stay public. Closing one workshop never triggers a review, and suspension never rewrites a workshop's own open or closed flag.

### Follow-through within the existing map

- Define production journals and traceability guarantees decides how a journal records edits so the integrity claim above can be kept.
- Define quotation and shared-order coordination rules decides quantities, allocations, and progress inside the audience rules above.
- Choose the exhibition journey, content, and visual direction decides how an approved profile, a verified certificate, and the unavailable notice are presented.
- Choose the technical architecture and reuse boundaries translates these actor, state, and audience rules into contracts. This ticket does not implement authentication or policies.

No new decision ticket is needed from this resolution.

title: Define the household, maker, workshop, and product model
description:
## Question

What do Household, Artisan, Workshop, and Product each mean in this digital exhibition, and what relationships does the first release need?

The SRS currently merges artisan and household, gives one account to one household, and defines a workshop as a physical location. Stress-test that model with a household containing several makers, several people contributing to one object, a household with more than one workshop, and a repeated product design versus an individual object or batch. Decide whose name and story appear publicly, who represents the household, what a product identity identifies, and how physical workshops relate to visits.

Keep the distinction between a domain identity and an authentication account explicit. Resolve only the relationships needed for the assignment; do not assume social profiles or add multi-village operation. Compare the current demo types and proposed data model, record accepted domain vocabulary in root GLOSSARY.md as it crystallises, and leave permission details and journal guarantees to their own decisions. The answer should define canonical terms, relationships, and meaningful examples rather than database tables.
close_reason: The human accepted all eight domain-model recommendations. Full resolution is in the ticket comments and canonical terms are in GLOSSARY.md.

comments.author: user
comments.text: Discussion checkpoint: the human accepted Household as the craft-producing unit presented under its own public name and history, and Artisan as an individual maker associated with a household. A household may include several artisans; its identity is independent of the person managing its account. These accepted terms are now in root GLOSSARY.md. The ticket remains in progress; representation, workshop relationships, product identity, and attribution still need discussion.

comments.author: user
comments.text: Discussion checkpoint: the human accepted Q2-Q4. First release has one designated representative account per household, each representing one household; the representative need not be a maker, and named artisans need no accounts for credit. A household may list several physical workshops, each with its own location and visiting information; listing on the map does not imply visitors may enter. Each Product identifies one physical object or one specific production batch, with its own QR code and journal. Repeating a design in another batch creates a separate Product; objects in a batch share the batch QR. Accepted domain terms were added to root GLOSSARY.md. Attribution, production versus visiting locations, and batch boundaries remain to discuss.

comments.author: user
comments.text:
## Resolution

The human accepted the recommendations in Q1, Q2-Q4, and Q5-Q8 during the live discussion. These decisions define the first-release domain relationships. Canonical vocabulary is recorded in root GLOSSARY.md.

### Household, artisan, and representation

- Household is the craft-producing unit presented under its own public name and history. It is the main public identity and can include several artisans.
- Artisan is an individual maker associated with a household. An artisan's name, contribution, and personal story can be distinguished from the household's collective history.
- Each household has one designated representative account for the first release, and that account represents one household. The representative may be an artisan or someone handling administration. Named artisans do not need accounts to receive credit.
- Household identity is independent of the representative account. Managing an account or uploading a journal does not automatically make someone a maker of the product.
- Every Product has one responsible Household. It may credit several artisans and their contributions, or credit the household's makers collectively when individual names are not supplied. Outside assistance can be acknowledged in the story while one household remains responsible.

Example: Gốm An is the household. Bình shapes a vase and Lan paints it, so both can receive maker credit. Another family member manages the account and uploads their account of the work without being presented as the vase's maker.

### Workshops and visiting

- Workshop is a physical craft location listed under a household. One household can list several workshops, each with its own location and visiting information.
- Map inclusion does not imply permission to enter. A production site and a place that welcomes visitors are distinct facts.
- A Product can name several production workshops of its responsible household. Its suggested visiting location is selected separately from a household location that welcomes visitors.

Example: Gốm An shapes a vase at one workshop, fires it at another, and welcomes visitors at its showroom. The production history names the production locations, while visitor directions lead to the showroom.

### Product identity, batches, and designs

- Each Product identifies one physical object or one specific Production batch. It has its own production history, journal, and QR code.
- A Production batch contains objects of one design made during one defined production run. A later run gets another Product identity even when the design is unchanged.
- Objects in a batch can share the batch's QR code. That code identifies the shared batch history rather than individually distinguishing every object within it.
- The number of objects represented by a batch is distinct from available stock. Selling or allocating some objects does not change which objects the batch identifies.
- Product design describes the repeatable appearance and characteristics shared by objects or batches. For the first release it remains descriptive information on each Product, which may be reused for a later batch. There is no separately managed design catalogue.

Examples: a unique vase is one Product representing one object. A March run of 300 blue cups is one Product representing a batch, and an April run of 200 cups of the same design is another Product with its own journal and QR code. Allocating 20 March cups does not redefine the March batch as 280 cups.

### Comparison with the assignment and current proposals

The binding assignment, docs/requirements/vCraft.pdf pages 2-4, requires household/workshop stories, product journals and QR storytelling, workshop visitor information, and wholesale work shared across households. It does not define a batch or separate household identity from a named maker.

The accepted model resolves these ambiguities in the proposals and demo:

- docs/SRS.md:50 merges household and artisan. apps/web/src/lib/demo/data.ts:33 combines a household name, one artisan name, and one workshop location in a single Artisan type. These concepts must remain distinct under the agreed vocabulary.
- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:375 already allows several workshops per household profile, but the demo flattens the location and the proposed trace response at docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:462 names a single workshop. Later contracts must preserve production locations separately from the visiting destination.
- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:405 attaches one trace code to a Product with stock, without defining object versus batch identity. The demo includes a 300-stock cup product with one code. That shared code is meaningful under the accepted model only when it identifies a particular production batch, not all future repetitions of a design.
- The proposed account-to-profile relationship does not replace Household identity, and the existing single artisan-name display is insufficient to express several makers' contributions.

### Follow-through within the existing map

- [Define approval, publishing, and access rules](vCRAFT-9hg.3) decides onboarding, permissions, and publication using the agreed representative relationship.
- [Define production journals and traceability guarantees](vCRAFT-9hg.4) decides journal timing, corrections, evidence, and QR lifecycle for the agreed object-or-batch identity. This resolution does not claim that a QR code proves who physically made an object.
- [Define quotation and shared-order coordination rules](vCRAFT-9hg.5) decides quotation quantities, allocations, and progress. The batch count and available quantity must remain distinct concepts.
- [Choose the exhibition journey, content, and visual direction](vCRAFT-9hg.6) decides presentation of household history, maker credit, production locations, and visitor directions.
- [Choose the technical architecture and reuse boundaries](vCRAFT-9hg.7) translates these relationships into contracts and persistence. This ticket does not prescribe tables or execute migrations.

No new decision ticket is needed from this resolution. The remaining questions belong to the existing named decisions. The map's unshaped questions and out-of-scope boundaries are unchanged.

comments.text:
Discovery findings, 28 October 2026

Read coverage: all 13 documents under docs. Main session read SRS.md, BRAND.md, all four files in docs/adr, all three docs/agents files, and the complete 1153-line moodboard.html. Read all four pages of requirements/vCraft.pdf visually in the local Chrome PDF viewer because text extraction tools were unavailable. A delegated read-only exploration read all 740 lines of ARCHITECTURE.md and all 492 lines of PLAN.md, then inspected implementation and installed dependencies. Also consulted README and confirmed no root glossary exists.

Original brief: three-person INT3306 course project, free technology choice, live demo and oral examination. The platform is a digital exhibition for a craft village, with household histories, products and production journals, QR storytelling pages, workshop map, wholesale quoting, and administrator coordination across households. These requirements support a story-led public experience while retaining operational workflows. The nine-week plan, AI assistant, extensive animation, and many detailed acceptance criteria are later planning choices, not all requirements of the four-page brief.

Product model: SRS lines 45-62 merges Artisan with Household and gives one account to one household. A Workshop is a physical location. Production Log entries belong to a Product. News is authored by village administrators. The existing model does not specify recurring public maker posts, follows, comments, conversations, or a visitor community. A social-space direction therefore needs decisions about participation, authorship, and content beyond a saleable product. BRAND section 1 already calls for a quiet museum-like experience, and its moodboard contains CSS/SVG illustrations and photo placeholders rather than real photography.

Implementation baseline: locale-prefixed public home, catalog and product detail, artisan list and profile, traceability, buyer quote workspace, and administrator allocation simulation exist. Web pages use apps/web/src/lib/demo/data.ts. Quote and allocation mutations remain component state. QR hash verification is real computation in apps/web/src/lib/hash-chain.ts, but no server persists it. The short QR redirect exists in apps/web/src/app/q/[code]/route.ts despite README marking it missing. Login, Studio, full map, and news pages are absent. No social entities or features exist. apps/api loads only HealthModule; apps/worker has an empty module. The database has an outbox entity and migrations for both drivers, not the business entities. API client is empty. Domain state machines and allocation validation are implemented; domain matching and traceability folders are empty, despite some documentation claims.

Stack baseline: installed Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind 4, NestJS 12/Fastify, MikroORM 7, Zod 4, Supabase libraries, Redis/BullMQ, shared UI and i18n packages, and test tooling in a pnpm/Turborepo monorepo. Many installed editor, animation, map, query and form dependencies are unused. The AI assistant has no implementation.
